Kenton Varda is candid that workerd's Durable Objects support is currently limited to a single instance; the goal is distributed, scalable operation.

2. What was not announced

This matters just as much. Do not fill in the gaps yourself:

  • There is no shutdown date for Deno Deploy, only "six months". Some posts estimate around April 2027, but that is not an official date.
  • Deno KV, Fresh and Subhosting are not addressed. If your service depends on Deno KV, there is no official migration path yet.
  • Migration support is promised to paying customers. Free projects are on their own.
  • Cloudflare says more announcements are coming in the next few months, so the details of self-hosted workerd are still to come.

3. What it means for technology choices

I read two signals here.

1. Long-term maintenance risk for independent runtimes is real. Deno is technically well regarded, but funding a runtime plus a hosting platform is hard. That does not mean Bun or any other newer runtime will follow the same path. It does mean "who maintains this, and what pays for it" deserves to be an explicit line in your evaluation, next to the benchmarks.

2. The Workers programming model is becoming portable. The most common objection to Cloudflare Workers has been lock-in: write your code the Workers way and it only runs on Cloudflare. If self-hosted workerd really becomes first-class, that objection shrinks a lot. For now, though, it is a stated direction, not a product you can evaluate.

4. Practical advice

If you run on Deno Deploy

  • Start your inventory now; do not wait for a shutdown date. List the Deno-specific features you rely on (Deno KV, for example) and find a replacement for each one.
  • The official destination is Cloudflare Workers. Node.js-compatible platforms are also an option, depending on how much your code depends on Deno APIs.
  • If you are a paying customer, reach out to Deno for migration help.

If you run the Deno runtime

  • You still get security updates for a year. No need to panic, but do not double down. For new projects, pick Node.js or a runtime your team already knows well.
  • Push code that depends on Deno.* APIs behind a thin adapter layer, so switching runtimes later means changing one place.
  • Packages published on JSR remain usable; JSR keeps running.

If you are evaluating Workers

  • Treat "we might self-host workerd later" as a bonus, not a deciding factor. Count it once there is a real product.

5. What it means for this site

8plus does not use Deno, so there is no direct impact. The site currently runs on Cloudflare Workers through vinext. When I moved it there, I kept the Next.js source and Vercel as a fallback precisely to avoid tying the site to a single platform. If self-hosted workerd matures, that is good news for exactly this kind of concern.

Runtime and hosting choices often get made early as a matter of taste, and only years later turn out to be business dependencies. Deno at least gave a year of runway and a clear direction, which is a responsible way to wind down. If you want to map which platform features your services depend on and how to keep an exit open, book a 30-minute intro call.

title: Deno 團隊加入 Cloudflare：Deno Deploy 剩半年，JavaScript runtime 該怎麼選
summary: 10/9 Deno 宣布整個團隊加入 Cloudflare：Deno runtime 再維護一年後停止開發，Deno Deploy 六個月後關閉。整理官方說了什麼、沒說什麼，以及現在用 Deno 的團隊該怎麼規劃。
html:
Deno 團隊加入 Cloudflare

10 月 9 日，Ryan Dahl 在 Deno 官方部落格發表 Deno is joining Cloudflare，Cloudflare 同步發了 Deno joins Cloudflare（Ryan Dahl 與 Kenton Varda 共同撰寫）。一句話：整個 Deno 團隊加入 Cloudflare，Deno runtime 與 Deno Deploy 都進入倒數。

這不是單純的併購新聞。對正在選 runtime 或部署平台的團隊來說，它直接改變了「Deno 是不是一個長期選項」的答案。

一、官方說了什麼

根據 Deno 的公告：

  • Deno runtime：再支援一年，期間每月發布包含 bug 修正與安全更新的版本；之後團隊停止開發 Deno runtime。程式碼維持開源，歡迎其他人接手。
  • Deno Deploy：再運作六個月，之後關閉。付費客戶搬到 Cloudflare Workers 會有遷移協助。
  • JSR（Deno 推的套件 registry）：繼續營運，基礎設施搬到 Cloudflare。
  • rusty_v8：持續維護，並朝整合進 workerd（Workers 的開源 runtime）的方向走。

Cloudflare 那篇則說明接下來的方向：由 Ryan Dahl 與 Bert Belder 帶隊，讓 workerd 自架成為正式支援的部署方式，並把 Deno 團隊做的 celld 的程式與設計合併回 workerd。Kenton Varda 也坦白，目前 workerd 的 Durable Objects 只支援單一實例，目標是做到分散式、可擴展。

二、官方沒說什麼

這部分同樣重要，規劃時不要自己補空白：

  • 沒有給 Deno Deploy 的關閉日期，只說「六個月」。網路上有人推算 2027 年 4 月左右，但那不是官方日期。
  • 沒有提到 Deno KV、Fresh、Subhosting 的後續。如果你的服務依賴 Deno KV，目前沒有官方遷移路徑。
  • 遷移協助只寫了付費客戶，免費專案要自己來。
  • Cloudflare 說「接下來幾個月會有更多公告」，所以自架 workerd 的細節還在路上。

三、這對選型代表什麼

我看到兩個訊號：

1. 獨立 runtime 的長期維護風險是真的。 Deno 在技術上很受好評，但商業上撐一個 runtime 加一個部署平台很難。這不代表 Bun 或其他新 runtime 會走一樣的路，但選型時「誰在維護、靠什麼收入維護」應該是一個明確的評估項目，不只是看效能跑分。

2. Workers 的程式模型正在變成「可以帶走」的東西。 過去選 Cloudflare Workers 最常見的顧慮是綁定：程式寫成 Workers 的樣子，就只能跑在 Cloudflare 上。如果 workerd 自架真的成為一等公民，這個顧慮會小很多。不過目前只是方向宣示，還沒有可以驗收的產品。

四、實務建議

用 Deno Deploy 的團隊

  • 現在就開始盤點，不要等關閉日期公告。列出用到的 Deno 專屬功能（例如 Deno KV），每一項先找到替代方案。
  • 官方指向的目的地是 Cloudflare Workers；Node.js 相容的平台也是選項，看你的程式碼對 Deno API 的依賴程度。
  • 付費客戶，主動聯絡 Deno 拿遷移協助。

用 Deno runtime 的團隊

  • 一年內仍有安全更新，不必恐慌，但不要再加碼。新專案建議選 Node.js 或你已經熟悉的 runtime。
  • 依賴 Deno.* API 的程式，盡量收斂到一層 adapter 後面，未來換 runtime 時只改一處。
  • 發佈在 JSR 的套件可以繼續用，JSR 會持續營運。

正在評估 Workers 的團隊

  • 把「未來可能自架 workerd」當加分，不要當成決策依據，等正式產品出來再算進去。

五、對這個站的影響

8plus 沒有用 Deno，所以沒有直接影響。這個站目前透過 vinext 部署在 Cloudflare Workers，搬遷時我保留了 Next.js 原始碼與 Vercel 當退路，就是不想把網站綁死在單一平台。workerd 自架如果成熟，對這種「不想被綁定」的考量是好消息。

runtime 和部署平台的選擇，常常在專案初期被當成技術偏好，幾年後才發現是商業依賴。Deno 這次至少給了一年緩衝和清楚的方向，算是負責任的收尾。如果你想盤點自己的服務綁了哪些平台功能、怎麼留退路，可以預約 30 分鐘初談。

title: The eMudhra intermediate CA key compromise: even if your site never used it, check your servers' trust stores
summary: On October 17 a researcher showed that the private keys of eight eMudhra intermediate CAs could be computed straight from the public certificates. Browsers blocked them within hours and Chrome and Mozilla pulled the root. Browsers are fine now; the trust stores in your servers, containers and CI are what need checking.
html:
The eMudhra intermediate CA key compromise

On October 17 a researcher told the major root programs that the private keys of eight intermediate CA certificates belonging to the Indian certificate authority eMudhra could be recovered. Mozilla described what happened on its security blog and in the Bugzilla incident, and Google published its own write-up for Chrome and Android.

Whoever holds an intermediate CA key can issue certificates browsers will accept for any domain. This wasn't one website having a bad day. It was a link in the HTTPS chain of trust breaking.

1. What happened

  • Eight intermediates were affected: six for TLS and two for code signing, all P-384 keys generated in the same batch on April 30, 2025.
  • Mozilla's investigation found that all eight private keys were integers smaller than 256. Given the public certificate, the key can be computed almost instantly, and Mozilla's engineers recovered them independently without any hints.
  • Timeline (UTC): Chrome received the report at 18:05 on 10/17 and blocked the keys via CRLSet at 19:45. Mozilla received it at 20:06 and finished its OneCRL block at 22:59. eMudhra revoked the eight certificates on 10/18, and Sectigo revoked its cross-signs on 10/19.
  • On 10/20 Mozilla shipped NSS 3.131.1, removing the root that signed these intermediates, emSign ECC Root CA - G3. Chrome's root store removal was expected to reach devices that rely on it on 10/27 (Pacific time).
  • In Bugzilla, eMudhra estimated about 30,000 certificates needed migrating, about 97% of them issued via ACME. Its October 28 update announced a wind-down of its publicly trusted TLS business.

The good news: Google says no TLS certificate chaining to these intermediates had been logged to Certificate Transparency before the block, so browsers that enforce CT could not have been fooled by a forged certificate.

2. Why ops teams still need to care

Browsers have automatic blocking channels. Your servers are not browsers.

Backend calls to third-party APIs, webhooks, crawlers and CI package downloads rely on the OS ca-certificates package, on trust stores bundled with language runtimes (Python's certifi, for example), or on whatever copy was frozen into a container image. Many non-browser clients don't check CT either.

The community-maintained tracking page noted on 10/28 that Apple's developer tools on macOS (git, curl, python3) still trusted these certificates at that point. Patch progress varies a lot between components, so "the browser is fine" doesn't mean you're fine.

3. Two groups, two jobs

A. Your site certificate was issued by eMudhra / emSign: the root is gone, so move to another CA now.

B. Everyone else: update the trust stores on servers, containers and developer machines.

# 1. Check who issued your site certificate (look for emSign / eMudhra)
echo | openssl s_client -connect example.com:443 -servername example.com 2>/dev/null \
  | openssl x509 -noout -issuer

# 2. Test whether a client still trusts the blocked intermediates (it should fail)
curl -sS -o /dev/null https://dv-g3b-emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com/ \
  && echo "still trusted, update needed" || echo "rejected (or a network error, double-check)"

# 3. Debian / Ubuntu hosts and containers
apt-get update && apt-get install --only-upgrade ca-certificates

# 4. Python projects
pip install -U certifi   # 2026.10.19 and later include the fix

4. Checklist

  • List the certificate issuer for every domain you run, including APIs and public endpoints of internal services
  • Update ca-certificates on servers and CI runners
  • Rebuild your Docker images, not just the hosts; the trust store inside an old image never changes on its own
  • Move Node.js to the October 21 security release (v26.12.1, v24.22.1 or v22.23.4); the official notice includes this CA update
  • Update certifi in Python projects, and remember Java keeps its own cacerts
  • Run the curl test above from production, not just your laptop
  • Behind a TLS-intercepting proxy, it's the proxy's trust store that counts, not the client's

5. My take

The lesson here is that a trust store is a dependency too. We watch package.json and lockfiles closely, yet few teams know how old the CA bundle inside their production containers is.

The other number worth noticing is the 97% issued through ACME. Certificate automation turns "switch CA" from a project into a config change, and how quickly affected sites can get out of this depends largely on whether they automated. If your certificates are still renewed by hand once a year, this is a good moment to change that.

If you want certificate, trust store and base image updates built into a regular operations routine, book a 30-minute intro call.

title: eMudhra 中繼 CA 私鑰外洩：你的網站沒用它，也該檢查伺服器的信任清單
summary: 10 月 17 日，研究人員發現 eMudhra 八張中繼 CA 憑證的私鑰可以直接從公開憑證算出來，瀏覽器數小時內封鎖、Chrome 與 Mozilla 隨後移除根憑證。瀏覽器已經沒事，真正要檢查的是你的伺服器、容器和 CI 裡的信任清單。
html:
eMudhra 中繼 CA 私鑰外洩

10 月 17 日，一位研究人員向各大根憑證計畫回報：印度憑證機構 eMudhra 有八張中繼 CA 憑證的私鑰可以被還原。Mozilla 在 安全部落格 與 Bugzilla 事件單 公開了經過，Google 也發了 Chrome 與 Android 的說明。

拿到中繼 CA 私鑰的人，可以替任何網域簽出瀏覽器會接受的憑證。這不是某個網站出事，而是整個 HTTPS 信任鏈的一環出事。

一、到底發生什麼事

  • 八張受影響的中繼憑證：6 張用於 TLS、2 張用於程式碼簽章，都是 2025 年 4 月 30 日同一批產生的 P-384 金鑰。
  • Mozilla 的調查指出，這八把私鑰都是小於 256 的整數。也就是說，只要有公開的憑證，就能幾乎瞬間算出私鑰。Mozilla 工程師沒有任何提示也能獨立還原。
  • 時間線（UTC）：10/17 18:05 Chrome 收到回報，19:45 透過 CRLSet 封鎖；Mozilla 20:06 收到回報，22:59 完成 OneCRL 封鎖。10/18 eMudhra 撤銷八張憑證，10/19 Sectigo 撤銷交叉簽章。
  • 10/20 Mozilla 發布 NSS 3.131.1，移除簽出這些中繼憑證的根憑證 emSign ECC Root CA - G3；Chrome Root Store 的移除則預計在 10/27（美西時間）推到使用它的裝置。
  • eMudhra 在 Bugzilla 估計約 30,000 張憑證要遷移，其中約 97% 透過 ACME 簽發；10/28 的官方更新則宣布逐步退出公開信任的 TLS 憑證業務。

好消息是：Google 表示封鎖前，沒有任何從這些中繼憑證簽出的 TLS 憑證被記錄到 Certificate Transparency，所以會強制檢查 CT 的瀏覽器不會被偽造憑證騙過。

二、為什麼維運團隊還要管

瀏覽器有自動更新的封鎖機制，但你的伺服器不是瀏覽器。

後端呼叫第三方 API、webhook、爬蟲、CI 下載套件，用的是作業系統的 ca-certificates、語言執行環境自帶的信任清單（例如 Python 的 certifi），或容器映像裡凍結的那一份。很多非瀏覽器用戶端也不檢查 CT。

社群整理的追蹤頁在 10/28 補充：macOS 上 Apple 的開發工具（git、curl、python3）當時仍信任這些憑證。換句話說，修補進度在不同元件之間差很多，不能假設「瀏覽器沒事就沒事」。

三、兩種人要做的事

A. 網站憑證是 eMudhra／emSign 簽發的：根憑證已被移除，要立刻換到其他 CA。

B. 其他所有人：更新伺服器、容器與開發機的信任清單。

# 1. 看自己網站憑證的發行者（找 emSign / eMudhra）
echo | openssl s_client -connect example.com:443 -servername example.com 2>/dev/null \
  | openssl x509 -noout -issuer

# 2. 測試用戶端是否還信任被封鎖的中繼憑證（應該連線失敗才對）
curl -sS -o /dev/null https://dv-g3b-emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com/ \
  && echo "仍然信任，需要更新" || echo "已拒絕（若是網路問題請再確認）"

# 3. Debian / Ubuntu 主機或容器
apt-get update && apt-get install --only-upgrade ca-certificates

# 4. Python 專案
pip install -U certifi   # 2026.10.19 之後的版本已處理

四、檢查清單

  • 盤點自己所有網域（含 API、內部服務對外的端點）的憑證發行者
  • 伺服器與 CI runner 更新 ca-certificates
  • 重建 Docker 映像，不要只更新主機；舊映像裡的信任清單不會自己變
  • Node.js 升到 10/21 安全更新的版本（v26.12.1／v24.22.1／v22.23.4），官方公告已包含這次的 CA 更新
  • Python 專案更新 certifi；Java 記得它有自己的 cacerts
  • 用上面的測試網址，從正式環境實際跑一次 curl
  • 有 TLS 攔截代理的環境，檢查的是代理的信任清單，不是用戶端

五、我的看法

這次事件提醒的是：信任清單也是相依套件。我們習慣盯 package.json 和 lockfile，卻很少有人知道正式環境的容器裡那份 CA bundle 是哪一天的版本。

另一個值得注意的數字是 97% 透過 ACME 簽發。憑證自動化讓「換一家 CA」從專案變成設定，這次受影響的網站能不能快速脫身，很大程度取決於當初有沒有做自動化。如果你的憑證還是一年手動換一次，現在是改掉的好時機。

title: GitHub Copilot connectors in public preview: MCP goes from install-it-yourself to sign-in-and-go. Set up the gates first
summary: On October 28, GitHub put Copilot connectors into public preview: 26 GitHub-verified MCP servers you connect once and use across Copilot surfaces. What changes, and the settings admins should check before rolling it out.
html:
GitHub Copilot connectors: MCP becomes sign-in-and-go

On October 28, GitHub announced that Copilot connectors are in public preview. Connectors are GitHub-verified MCP servers, and 26 services are available at launch, including Slack, Figma, Notion, Sentry, Linear, Atlassian Rovo, Cloudflare, Vercel and Work IQ.

Until now, getting Copilot to read a Slack thread or a Sentry error meant finding an MCP server, setting up sign-in, and repeating that for every tool. Now you pick a service, sign in once, and you are done.

1. What actually changes

Based on the changelog and the official docs:

  1. No install, no manual credentials. GitHub handles MCP server configuration and authentication, and Copilot keeps you signed in in the background.
  2. Connect once, use everywhere. The same connection works in the Copilot app, Copilot CLI (the Connectors tab under /mcp), VS Code, Copilot in the cloud and GitHub Mobile.
  3. No need to name the service. Once connected, Copilot uses a service's tools whenever they are relevant to the request.
  4. Scheduled work. In the Copilot app you can set up automations that use a connected service on a schedule.
  5. Available on all Copilot plans, but still in public preview, and the docs say it is subject to change.

One current limitation: connectors are not yet supported in sessions that run on GitHub Actions, such as assigning an issue to Copilot. Local and cloud sandbox sessions work.

2. How I read it

The barrier to MCP moves from engineering to a click

MCP is already how many agents reach external tools, but setup has always been the hurdle. Connectors remove that step, so people on the team who do not write code can now point Copilot at Slack, Notion or Linear. That speeds up adoption and creates a new governance problem: knowing how to install an MCP server used to be a filter in itself. It no longer is.

"Verified" does not mean "safe to expose all your data"

GitHub verifies the MCP server itself. A connector connects with the identity you signed in and approved, so what the agent can read or write essentially follows your permissions in that service. If someone can see a lot of Slack channels, connecting a connector widens what Copilot can reach by the same amount.

The governance controls arrived first

In August, GitHub made MCP allowlists in enterprise managed settings generally available. You define allowedMcpServers and deniedMcpServers in copilot/managed-settings.json in your .github-private repository, matching by URL (wildcards supported), local command, or name. A malformed configuration fails closed and is blocked. The changelog also notes that name matching is a convenience, not a security control, because users can rename servers.

3. Pre-rollout checklist for Business and Enterprise admins

According to the docs, all of these need to be right before an organization can use connectors:

  1. The Editor preview features policy must be enabled, since connectors are in preview.
  2. The MCP servers in Copilot policy must be enabled, or connectors will not work.
  3. If Restrict MCP access to registry servers is set to "Registry only", clients that enforce it will block connectors. It has to be "Allow all".
  4. The allowlist must include each connector's URL, or a matching wildcard.
  5. Deny wins. A matching deniedMcpServers entry blocks a connector even if the allowlist permits it.
  6. The service side has to allow it too. Some services need their own admin to enable access first, such as turning on MCP access in Slack.

4. Recommendations for teams

  • Decide the allowlist before turning on preview features. Do not flip on "Allow all" for a trial and forget to tighten it. Pick two or three services you actually need, such as Sentry and Linear, and deny the rest.
  • Start with read-only work. Investigating errors, summarizing threads and collecting requirements are low-risk with obvious payoff. Hold off on uses that write data or send messages until the workflow is stable.
  • Review permissions in each service. A connector's reach equals the user's access in that service. Use this as a reason to clean up sensitive Slack channels and Notion pages that are visible to the whole company.
  • Track who connected what. The feature will keep changing during preview. At minimum, know internally which people and repositories are using which connectors.

MCP is moving from an engineer's tool to a default feature for everyone. The hard part is not whether you can connect, but which data an agent should be allowed to touch. If you want help planning MCP and Copilot governance settings for your team, book a 30-minute intro call.

title: GitHub Copilot connectors 公開預覽：MCP 從「自己裝」變成「登入就能用」，企業該先設好閘門
summary: GitHub 10 月 28 日推出 Copilot connectors 公開預覽，首批 26 個服務、由 GitHub 驗證的 MCP server，登入一次就能在各個 Copilot 介面使用。整理它改變了什麼，以及管理者上線前該確認的設定。
html:
GitHub Copilot connectors：MCP 變成「登入就能用」

10 月 28 日，GitHub 在 changelog 宣布 Copilot connectors 進入公開預覽。connectors 是由 GitHub 驗證過的 MCP server，首批 26 個服務，包括 Slack、Figma、Notion、Sentry、Linear、Atlassian Rovo、Cloudflare、Vercel、Work IQ 等。

以前要讓 Copilot 讀 Slack 討論串或 Sentry 錯誤，得自己找 MCP server、設定登入，每個工具重來一次。現在是選服務、登入一次，就結束了。

一、具體改變了什麼

依照 changelog 與官方文件：

  1. 不用安裝、不用手動填憑證：GitHub 負責 MCP server 的設定與驗證，Copilot 會在背景維持登入狀態。
  2. 連一次，到處都能用：同一個連線可以在 Copilot app、Copilot CLI（/mcp 裡的 Connectors 分頁）、VS Code、Copilot in the cloud 和 GitHub Mobile 使用。
  3. 不必指名：連好之後，只要跟需求相關，Copilot 會自己決定要不要呼叫那個服務的工具。
  4. 可以排程：在 Copilot app 裡能建立自動化，定期用連線的服務處理例行工作。
  5. 適用所有 Copilot 方案，但仍是公開預覽，官方文件註明功能可能變動。

目前有一個限制：在 GitHub Actions 上跑的 session（例如把 issue 指派給 Copilot）還不支援 connectors；本機與雲端沙箱 session 則可以用。

二、我怎麼解讀

MCP 的門檻從「工程」變成「點擊」

MCP 已經是很多 agent 接外部工具的方式，但門檻一直在安裝與設定。connectors 把這一步拿掉，意味著團隊裡不寫程式的人，也能讓 Copilot 去讀 Slack、Notion、Linear。對採用速度是好事，對管控則是新的考驗：以前「會裝 MCP」本身就是一道過濾，現在沒有了。

「已驗證」不等於「可以放心給所有資料」

GitHub 驗證的是 MCP server 本身。connector 是用你自己登入、授權的身分去連服務，所以 agent 能讀到什麼、寫入什麼，基本上跟著你在該服務上的權限走。一個在 Slack 看得到很多頻道的人連上 connector，Copilot 能碰到的範圍也就跟著變大。資料範圍要從各服務的權限去管，不是靠 connector 名單。

治理工具其實已經先到位

GitHub 8 月已經讓 MCP allowlist 進入企業 managed settings，並正式推出：在 .github-private repo 的 copilot/managed-settings.json 裡設定 allowedMcpServers 和 deniedMcpServers，可以用 URL（支援萬用字元）、本機指令或名稱比對，設定格式錯誤時會「fail closed」直接擋下。changelog 也特別提醒，名稱比對只是方便用，不算安全控管，因為使用者可以改名。

三、Business／Enterprise 管理者上線前的檢查清單

依官方文件，組織要用 connectors，以下設定都要對：

  1. Editor preview features 政策要開啟（因為還在預覽）。
  2. MCP servers in Copilot 政策要開啟，否則 connectors 不會運作。
  3. Restrict MCP access to registry servers 若設成「Registry only」，在有執行此設定的用戶端上會擋掉 connectors，要改成「Allow all」才能用。
  4. allowlist 要加入每個 connector 的 URL（或對應的萬用字元）。
  5. denylist 優先：只要符合 deniedMcpServers，即使 allowlist 允許也會被擋。
  6. 服務端也要開：有些服務需要它自己的管理者先允許，例如 Slack 要先開放 MCP 存取。

四、給台灣團隊的建議

  • 先決定白名單，再開預覽功能。不要為了試用把「Allow all」打開就忘了收。先挑兩三個真正有需求的服務（例如 Sentry、Linear），其他的用 deny 擋住。
  • 從唯讀場景開始。查錯誤、摘要討論串、整理需求，這類讀取型任務風險低、效益明顯。會寫入或發訊息的用法，等流程穩定再開。
  • 盤點各服務的權限。connector 的資料範圍等於使用者在該服務的權限。趁這次把 Slack、Notion 裡「全公司可見」的敏感頻道和頁面整理一遍。
  • 記錄誰連了什麼。預覽階段功能還會變，至少內部要知道哪些人、哪些 repo 在用哪些 connector。

MCP 正在從工程師的工具變成每個人的預設功能。真正要花心思的，不是連不連得上，而是哪些資料該讓 agent 碰。如果你想替團隊規劃 MCP 與 Copilot 的治理設定，可以預約 30 分鐘初談。

title: Google Cloud's London power incident report: one zone went dark, so why did the whole region hurt?
summary: On October 20 the facility behind Google Cloud's europe-west2-b lost power, and the backup generators never started because of a controller misconfiguration. Impact lasted 6 hours 8 minutes. The incident report published on October 27 is worth reading for anyone running services in the cloud, especially the part about multi-zone setups.
html:
Google Cloud's London power incident report

On October 20, zone b of Google Cloud's London region, europe-west2, lost power entirely, and the impact spread to the other zones in the region. On October 27 Google posted a full incident report on its status page, and it is refreshingly candid.

Most of us don't run anything in London, but the report describes a problem every cloud architecture runs into eventually: redundancy doesn't always work at the moment you need it.

1. How it happened

The facility normally runs 2N power: two utility feeds that can each carry the full load, backed by diesel generators and five minutes of UPS battery.

  1. A routine quarterly generator load test on October 14 surfaced issues, so feed B was opened for repairs, leaving the site temporarily on feed A alone (1N).
  2. At 22:53 Pacific on October 19, an underground cable fault outside the facility cut feed A.
  3. The generator controllers (PLCs) decided whether to start the generators by sensing voltage upstream of the open feed B breaker. Feed B was disconnected, but its upstream side was still live, so the PLCs concluded utility power was healthy and never started the generators.
  4. The UPS carried the load until the batteries ran out, and the whole zone lost power from 23:00. On-site staff eventually switched the facility to a standby utility source by hand.

Standby power was connected within an hour, but services didn't come straight back. A large number of storage devices had shut down uncleanly and needed recovery first, and Google chose not to rush traffic back in and make things worse. From start to recovery of most workloads, the incident lasted 6 hours 8 minutes.

2. The part worth reading twice: why the other zones suffered

In theory, when one zone fails the other two (a and c) absorb the load. The report names two reasons that didn't go smoothly:

  • A sudden demand surge: huge numbers of workloads failed over to zones a and c at once, exhausting compute capacity and causing queuing, delayed database failovers and intermittent 500 and 503 errors. The report admits that some failovers failed because of capacity constraints.
  • Control-plane dependencies across zones: regional services called metadata components sitting in zone b and timed out. During this window some customers couldn't create, update or delete regional resources.

Google is also clear that zonal resources (VMs, non-HA Cloud SQL, zonal GKE clusters and so on) being unavailable during a zone failure is working as designed. If you need failover, planning cross-zone recovery is your job.

3. What you can check today

On GCP, start by finding the resources that actually live in a single zone:

# Cloud SQL: availabilityType ZONAL means no cross-zone HA
gcloud sql instances list \
  --format="table(name,region,gceZone,settings.availabilityType)"

# GKE: if location is a zone (e.g. us-central1-b), it's a zonal cluster
gcloud container clusters list --format="table(name,location)"

# Which zones your VMs are spread across
gcloud compute instances list --format="table(name,zone.basename(),status)"

The same applies on any cloud. The checklist:

  • Map which zones each service's database, cache and compute run in
  • Write down which services truly need cross-zone resilience and which can tolerate a few hours of downtime
  • Don't build a failover plan that depends on creating new resources mid-incident; the control plane may be struggling and capacity may already be gone
  • Keep a backup copy in another region, and actually rehearse restoring it
  • During maintenance (database upgrades, node swaps), notice when you've temporarily dropped to a single copy
  • Subscribe to your provider's status feed and run your own external monitoring

4. My take

The root cause is very much a data center problem, but the lesson is a software one: a misconfiguration that only triggers in a maintenance state is invisible to everyday testing. Google's own action items include freezing planned maintenance at other sites with a similar topology and reviewing comparable PLC configurations worldwide by November 15.

Small teams don't need to go fully multi-region. But you should know which services are single points of failure, how long they'd be down, and who decides to fail over. Writing that down on one page is more practical than paying for another zone.
