title: Google Cloud 倫敦區域停電事後報告：單一可用區掛掉，為什麼整個區域都受傷
summary: 10 月 20 日 Google Cloud europe-west2-b 機房停電，備援發電機因控制器設定錯誤沒有啟動，影響持續 6 小時 8 分。10/27 公布的事後報告值得每個在雲端跑服務的團隊讀一遍，尤其是「多可用區」那段。
html:
Google Cloud 倫敦區域停電事後報告

10 月 20 日（台灣時間下午兩點左右），Google Cloud 倫敦區域 europe-west2 的 b 可用區整個斷電，影響一路延伸到同區域的其他可用區。Google 在 10 月 27 日於狀態頁公布完整的事後報告，寫得相當坦白。

我們多數人不會在倫敦跑服務，但這份報告講的是每個雲端架構都會遇到的問題：備援在真正需要的時候，不一定會動。

一、事情怎麼發生的

這個機房原本是 2N 供電，也就是兩路市電各自能扛全部負載，後面還有柴油發電機和 5 分鐘的 UPS 電池。

  1. 10 月 14 日例行的季度發電機負載測試發現問題，機房把 B 路市電斷開維修，暫時只剩 A 路一條（1N）。
  2. 10 月 19 日 22:53（美西時間），機房外的地下電纜故障，A 路斷電。
  3. 發電機控制器（PLC）判斷要不要啟動發電機時，量的是 B 路斷路器上游的電壓。B 路雖然已經斷開，上游仍有電，PLC 就以為「市電正常」，沒有啟動發電機。
  4. UPS 撐到電池耗盡，23:00 起整個可用區斷電。現場人員最後手動切到備用市電，才恢復供電。

斷電後不到一小時，備用市電就接上了，但服務沒有馬上回來。大量儲存設備是非正常關機，必須先完成修復，Google 選擇不急著開放流量以免狀況更糟。從開始到多數工作負載恢復，總共 6 小時 8 分。

二、最值得看的：其他可用區為什麼也受傷

照理說，一個可用區掛掉，另外兩個（a、c）應該頂住。報告直接寫了兩個原因：

  • 需求瞬間湧入：大量工作負載同時容錯移轉到 a、c，把運算容量吃滿，造成排隊、資料庫容錯移轉延遲，以及間歇性的 500／503 錯誤。報告也承認，部分容錯移轉因為容量不足而失敗。
  • 控制平面跨可用區相依：區域層級的服務會去呼叫位在 b 區的中繼資料元件，結果逾時。這段期間，有些客戶無法建立、更新或刪除區域資源。

Google 也說得很清楚：單一可用區的資源（VM、非 HA 的 Cloud SQL、zonal GKE 叢集等）在可用區故障時無法使用，是「設計如此」；需要容錯的話，客戶要自己規劃跨可用區的復原機制。

三、你現在可以檢查的事

如果你用 GCP，先找出哪些資源其實只活在一個可用區：

# Cloud SQL：availabilityType 為 ZONAL 代表沒有跨可用區 HA
gcloud sql instances list \
  --format="table(name,region,gceZone,settings.availabilityType)"

# GKE：location 是 zone（例如 asia-east1-b）就是 zonal 叢集
gcloud container clusters list --format="table(name,location)"

# VM 分布在哪些可用區
gcloud compute instances list --format="table(name,zone.basename(),status)"

其他雲也一樣，重點是這張清單：

  • 列出每個服務的資料庫、快取、運算各在哪些可用區
  • 區分「真的需要跨可用區」和「可以接受停幾小時」的服務，寫下來
  • 容錯計畫不要依賴事故當下建立新資源；控制平面可能正忙、容量可能被搶光
  • 確認備份在另一個區域也有一份，並實際演練還原
  • 進行維護（升級資料庫、換節點）時，留意自己是不是暫時降到「只剩一份」
  • 訂閱雲端廠商狀態頁的 RSS／通知，並有自己的外部監測

四、我的看法

這次的根本原因很「機房」，但教訓很軟體：一個在維護狀態下才會觸發的設定錯誤，平常的測試完全測不到。 Google 自己的改善項目也包括在其他類似架構的機房凍結計畫性維護，以及在 11 月 15 日前檢查全球同類 PLC 設定。

對中小團隊來說，不必追求全面多區域。但至少要知道哪些服務是單點、出事時要停多久、誰來決定切換。把這些寫成一頁文件，比多買一個可用區更實際。

如果你想檢視現有架構的單點與復原計畫，可以預約 30 分鐘初談。

title: Let an AI agent trim your JavaScript: the Next.js 16.4 bundle optimizer and the new Bundle Analyzer
summary: On October 28, Next.js released the next-bundle-optimizer agent skill and new Bundle Analyzer tools. Vercel says it cut nearly 2 MB of compressed JavaScript across v0 and vercel.com. How it works, what it requires, and what to watch for when your team adopts it.
html:
Let an AI agent trim your JavaScript

On October 28, the Next.js blog published Ship less JavaScript in Next.js with your AI agent, by Will Binns-Smith. It has two halves: a next-bundle-optimizer skill for AI agents, and a set of new Bundle Analyzer features for humans.

What makes it worth writing about is not "AI can do one more thing". It is the division of labor it demonstrates: the tool does the analysis, the agent makes the change, and people sign off.

1. The problem: you think it is lazy-loaded, but it is not

The official example is a classic. You write lazy(() => import('./HeavyComponent')) to defer a large component. If that is the only module importing HeavyComponent, the deferral works. But if any other module in the same bundle imports it statically, the code still loads upfront.

This is hard to catch by reading code, because the two imports can live in completely unrelated files. The bigger the project, the more quietly it grows.

2. How the agent skill works

  • Requirements: Next.js 16.4 with Turbopack, the default bundler since Next.js 16, because the skill relies on Turbopack's module graph.
  • Install: npx skills add vercel/next.js --skill next-bundle-optimizer, then run /next-bundle-optimizer in your agent.
  • Approach: the agent exports saved next analyze snapshots as JSON, rebuilds the module and chunk graphs, finds large groups of connected modules, and uses minimum cut to find a small set of import boundaries that would defer them. It then checks the proposal against your source code and how the components are actually used.
  • It also finds: logic that could move to React Server Components, duplicate versions of large dependencies, and places where tree shaking failed and pulled in unused code.
  • Report-only by default. To apply changes, run /next-bundle-optimizer fix, which reruns the analysis and compares snapshots before and after.

3. Vercel's own numbers

Vercel says the skill saved nearly 2 MB of compressed JavaScript across v0 and vercel.com. Some of the specific findings:

  • An experimental code editor in v0 loaded on nearly every page, even for users outside the experiment: 150 KB saved on most pages.
  • v0's centralized dialog registry eagerly loaded heavy dialogs: 40–650 KB saved depending on the page.
  • On vercel.com, markdown rendering, syntax highlighting and charts for the Agent panel shipped even when the panel was closed: 255 KB saved on the dashboard page.
  • A URL parsing helper, imported through a shared utility file, pulled in the entire observability query engine: 125 KB saved on the deployments page.

These are numbers from Vercel's own large products, not a promise for yours. The process is the part worth copying: every change went through a pull request and was verified on a preview deployment before shipping.

4. The Bundle Analyzer for humans

If you would rather dig in yourself, next analyze gained some useful features:

  • Route summary: the home view lists your largest client routes, so you know where to start.
  • Automatic snapshots and diffs: every analysis is saved, so you can measure an optimization or find out what a new feature or dependency added.
  • Critical render path: modules loaded synchronously for the initial render are highlighted, and async dependencies can be filtered out. The post also notes you should still test which modules really are on the critical path.
  • Graph data can be exported for your own tooling with next analyze export.

5. Adoption advice

  1. Measure before you optimize. Add a bundle-size budget check to CI; otherwise the weight comes back a month after the agent removes it.
  2. Start in report mode. Let the agent list problems and suggestions, and have a person decide whether to run fix.
  3. One change per pull request, and click through the interactions on a preview deployment before merging. Deferring code can change what users experience on their first click.
  4. Confirm your build uses Turbopack. If the project is still pinned to webpack, the skill will not work.

6. What it means for this site

8plus is already on Next.js 16.4 and has its own bundle budget check (pnpm check:bundle). It measures the gzip size of the JavaScript each page loads initially, with a 200 KB target and a 340 KB ceiling; the home page baseline recorded on October 1 was 324 KB. In other words, there is still a gap to the target, which is exactly where tools like this help.

One caveat: in production, this site is built with Vite through vinext and runs on Cloudflare Workers, while next analyze analyzes the Turbopack build. The two may not split code the same way, so anything found there needs to be verified again against what is actually deployed.

JavaScript size is the kind of technical debt that grows a little at a time and is substantial a year later. Finding the cause used to take a senior engineer an afternoon of tracing imports; now an agent can produce the first report. The tooling got cheap. Budgets and sign-off are what the team still has to own. If you want help setting up performance budgets and checks for your site, book a 30-minute intro call.

title: 讓 AI agent 幫你瘦身 JavaScript：Next.js 16.4 的 bundle optimizer 與新版 Bundle Analyzer
summary: Next.js 10/28 推出 next-bundle-optimizer agent skill 與新版 Bundle Analyzer，Vercel 說在 v0 與 vercel.com 上砍掉將近 2 MB 的壓縮後 JavaScript。整理它怎麼運作、前提條件，以及團隊導入時該注意什麼。
html:
讓 AI agent 幫你瘦身 JavaScript

10 月 28 日，Next.js 官方部落格發表 Ship less JavaScript in Next.js with your AI agent（Will Binns-Smith）。內容分兩半：一個給 AI agent 用的 next-bundle-optimizer skill，和一組給人用的 Bundle Analyzer 新功能。

我覺得這篇值得寫，不是因為「AI 又能做一件事」，而是它示範了一個很實際的分工：分析交給工具，修改交給 agent，驗收留給人。

一、問題：你以為延遲載入了，其實沒有

官方舉的例子很典型：你用 lazy(() => import('./HeavyComponent')) 想延後載入一個大元件。如果它是唯一引用 HeavyComponent 的地方，延遲會生效；但只要同一個 bundle 裡任何其他模組靜態 import 了它，這段程式碼照樣會在一開始就載入。

這種問題很難靠讀程式碼發現，因為兩個 import 可能在完全不相干的檔案裡。專案越大，越容易默默變胖。

二、agent skill 怎麼運作

  • 前提：Next.js 16.4，而且要用 Turbopack（Next.js 16 起的預設 bundler），因為它依賴 Turbopack 的模組圖。
  • 安裝：npx skills add vercel/next.js --skill next-bundle-optimizer，然後在 agent 裡執行 /next-bundle-optimizer。
  • 做法：agent 把 next analyze 的快照匯出成 JSON，重建模組與 chunk 的關係圖，找出彼此相連的大型模組群，再用 minimum cut 找出「改少數幾個 import 邊界就能延後載入」的位置，最後對照原始碼確認元件實際怎麼被使用。
  • 還能抓：可以搬到 React Server Components 的邏輯、重複版本的大型依賴、tree shaking 沒生效而拉進未使用程式碼的情況。
  • 預設只報告。要套用修改得跑 /next-bundle-optimizer fix，它會重跑分析並比較前後快照。

三、Vercel 自己的數字

官方說用這個 skill 在 v0 與 vercel.com 上總共省下將近 2 MB 的壓縮後 JavaScript。幾個具體案例：

  • v0 有個實驗性程式碼編輯器，連不在實驗組的使用者也會載入，大部分頁面省下 150 KB。
  • v0 的集中式對話框註冊表，依頁面不同省下 40–650 KB。
  • vercel.com 的 Agent 面板沒打開也會載入 markdown、語法高亮與圖表，dashboard 頁省下 255 KB。
  • 一個 URL 解析工具透過共用檔案拉進了整個 observability 查詢引擎，deployments 頁省下 125 KB。

注意這些是 Vercel 自家大型產品的數字。每個修改都開成 PR、在 preview 部署上驗證後才上線，這個流程比數字本身更值得抄。

四、給人用的 Bundle Analyzer

不想交給 agent 的話，next analyze 也多了幾個實用功能：

  • 路由總覽：首頁直接列出最大的 client 路由，知道從哪裡開始查。
  • 自動快照與比對：每次分析自動存快照，可以 diff，量測優化成效或找出新功能帶來的成長。
  • 關鍵渲染路徑：標出初次渲染同步載入的模組，可以過濾掉非同步依賴。官方也提醒，實際哪些模組在關鍵路徑上，還是要自己測。
  • 圖資料可以用 next analyze export 匯出給自己的工具。

五、導入建議

  1. 先量，再優化。在 CI 加一個 bundle 大小的預算檢查，否則 agent 修完、下個月又長回來。
  2. 先用報告模式。讓 agent 列出問題與建議，人看過再決定要不要 fix。
  3. 一個修改一個 PR，在 preview 環境實際點過互動再合併。延後載入可能改變使用者第一次點擊時的體驗。
  4. 確認你的建置用的是 Turbopack。如果專案還鎖在 webpack，這個 skill 用不了。

六、對這個站的影響

8plus 已經在 Next.js 16.4，也有一個自己寫的 bundle 預算檢查（pnpm check:bundle），量的是各頁初次載入的 JavaScript gzip 大小，目標 200 KB、上限 340 KB，10/1 記錄的首頁基準是 324 KB。換句話說，離目標還有距離，這類工具正好派得上用場。

但有一個要注意的地方：這個站正式環境是透過 vinext 用 Vite 建置後跑在 Cloudflare Workers 上，而 next analyze 分析的是 Turbopack 的建置結果。兩者的切分方式不一定相同，所以在這裡找到的問題要回到實際部署的版本再驗證一次。

JavaScript 體積是那種「每次只多一點、一年後很可觀」的技術債。過去要找到原因得靠資深工程師花一個下午追 import，現在可以先讓 agent 跑一輪報告。工具變便宜了，預算與驗收才是團隊要守住的部分。如果你想幫自己的網站建立效能預算與檢查流程，可以預約 30 分鐘初談。

title: Agent Skills moves to the Agentic AI Foundation: skills become a cross-tool standard, so manage them like code
summary: On October 22, Anthropic donated the Agent Skills standard to the Agentic AI Foundation under the Linux Foundation, the same neutral home as MCP. What the donation actually covers, what is still open, and the ground rules a team should set before it starts building up skills.
html:
Agent Skills moves to the Agentic AI Foundation

On October 22, Anthropic announced it is donating Agent Skills to the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF). AAIF sits under the Linux Foundation and was co-founded by Anthropic, Block and OpenAI, and MCP was donated to it in December 2025. So the standard for how an agent reaches external tools (MCP) and the standard for how an agent learns a way of doing a task (Skills) now live in the same neutral place.

There is no new feature here. But for teams adopting coding agents, it answers a practical question: will the skills we write still work if we switch tools?

1. What the donation covers

According to Anthropic's announcement:

  1. What is donated: the Agent Skills standard itself, its name and logo, the GitHub organization, and the agentskills.io domain.
  2. Who maintains it: engineers from Anthropic, Google, OpenAI and other companies, participating as individuals. The lead maintainers are David Soria Parra and Mahesh Murag.
  3. How to take part: you do not need to join AAIF to use or contribute to the standard. Spec discussion happens on GitHub and Discord.
  4. Adoption so far: since the standard was published in December 2025, more than 70 agent platforms have integrated it, including ChatGPT, Cursor, GitHub Copilot and VS Code. One million skills have been published and nearly 280 million installed. These are Anthropic's own figures.
  5. What comes next: the proposed roadmap starts with versioned releases, a formal proposal process, and security guidance for people who write and install skills.

The format itself has not changed. Per the agentskills.io specification, a skill is a folder that must contain a SKILL.md, whose frontmatter needs at least a name (up to 64 characters, lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, matching the folder name) and a description (up to 1,024 characters). It can also include scripts/, references/ and assets/. At startup an agent reads only each skill's name and description; it loads the full instructions when a task matches, and reads bundled files or runs scripts only when needed.

2. What is still open

  • No timeline. Versioned releases, the proposal process and the security guidance are all still proposals. The announcement gives no dates.
  • "Supported" does not mean "behaves the same." Seventy-plus integrations do not guarantee identical behavior. The spec's allowed-tools field, which pre-approves the tools a skill may use, is itself marked experimental, and implementations may differ.
  • No security guidance yet. Skills can bundle executable scripts, and installs are in the hundreds of millions. Until the guidance lands, reviewing and publishing skills is each team's own responsibility.
  • The numbers are self-reported. The one million and 280 million figures come from Anthropic, with no independent source to check them against.

3. How I read it

Skills go from tool configuration to team asset

Instruction files written for a particular agent tend to get treated as personal settings: they sit in someone's home directory and get rewritten when the team changes tools. With the standard under neutral governance, it is easier to treat skills as shared, repo-tracked assets. It is the same shift teams made when CI configs and lint rules moved into version control.

The value is in the practice, not the format

The format is simple. The hard part is the content: how your team ships, how it reviews, where it looks first when something breaks. That knowledge usually lives in a wiki, in senior engineers' heads and in old Slack threads. Whether an agent does the right thing depends largely on whether those practices are written down. Standardization solves "write once, use anywhere." It does not solve "what to write."

Skills are part of your supply chain

A skill can ship Bash or Python scripts, and the agent will run them as instructed. From a risk perspective, installing a skill of unknown origin is a lot like running npm install on a package you have never looked at, and arguably more direct, because what executes it is an agent that makes its own decisions.

4. A checklist before your team starts accumulating skills

  1. Put them in version control. Shared skills live in the repo or a dedicated skills repo, and changes go through PR review rather than living on individual laptops.
  2. Read external skills before installing them, especially anything in scripts/. Try unfamiliar skills in a sandbox or an environment without production credentials.
  3. Write precise descriptions. The agent decides whether to activate a skill from its description. Too broad and it fires when it should not; too narrow and it never fires. The spec recommends stating both what the skill does and when to use it.
  4. One skill, one job. The spec suggests keeping SKILL.md under 500 lines and moving detail into references/. A do-everything skill is hard to maintain and hard to review.
  5. Do not rely on experimental fields for access control. allowed-tools is still experimental. Real permission boundaries belong in the agent platform, the sandbox and the credentials themselves.
  6. Validate the format with the official tool. The spec provides skills-ref validate to check frontmatter and naming, which fits nicely into CI.
  7. Watch for AAIF's security guidance. When it ships, review your existing skills and install process against it.

5. How this matches my own setup

The repo behind this site carries a fair number of agent skills for planning, development and review. In my experience, the difference between a good skill and a weak one is almost always whether the implicit judgment calls are written down: when to stop and ask a human, and when to just proceed. That is also where AI adoption deserves the most time. Spell out how people actually do the work first, then hand it to the machine.

If your concern is which external systems an agent can reach, see my earlier post on Copilot connectors and MCP governance. Skills govern how an agent works; connectors govern what it can touch. You need both.

With a shared standard, writing a skill once and using it across several agents becomes realistic. What to write, who can change it and which outside skills to trust are still decisions your team has to make. If you want help shaping your team's first set of skills or planning an agent rollout, book a 30-minute intro call.

title: Agent Skills 捐給 Agentic AI Foundation：skill 變成跨工具的標準格式，團隊該把它當程式碼管
summary: Anthropic 10 月 22 日把 Agent Skills 標準捐給 Linux Foundation 旗下的 Agentic AI Foundation，和 MCP 放在同一個中立組織。整理這次捐贈實際包含什麼、還沒說清楚的地方，以及團隊開始累積 skills 前該先定好的規矩。
html:
Agent Skills 捐給 Agentic AI Foundation：skill 變成跨工具的標準

10 月 22 日，Anthropic 宣布把 Agent Skills 捐給 Agentic AI Foundation（AAIF）。AAIF 隸屬 Linux Foundation，是 Anthropic 和 Block、OpenAI 共同成立的組織，MCP 在 2025 年 12 月就已經捐到這裡。換句話說，「agent 怎麼連外部工具」（MCP）和「agent 怎麼學會一件事的做法」（Skills），現在都放在同一個中立的地方維護。

這件事沒有新功能，但對正在導入 coding agent 的團隊來說，它回答了一個實際問題：我們寫的 skill，換工具之後還能不能用？

一、這次捐贈實際包含什麼

依 Anthropic 的公告：

  1. 捐出的內容：Agent Skills 標準本身，加上名稱與 logo、GitHub organization，以及 agentskills.io 網域。
  2. 維護方式：由來自 Anthropic、Google、OpenAI 等公司的工程師以個人身分參與維護，Lead Maintainer 是 David Soria Parra 與 Mahesh Murag。
  3. 參與門檻：使用或貢獻這個標準不需要加入 AAIF。規格討論在 GitHub 與 Discord。
  4. 採用現況：公告說自 2025 年 12 月公開標準以來，已有超過 70 個 agent 平台整合，點名了 ChatGPT、Cursor、GitHub Copilot 和 VS Code；目前已發布 100 萬個 skills，安裝次數接近 2.8 億。這些是 Anthropic 自己公布的數字。
  5. 接下來的方向：提議的 roadmap 先處理三件事：版本化發布、正式的提案流程，以及給 skill 作者與安裝者的安全指引。

格式本身沒有變。依 agentskills.io 的規格，一個 skill 就是一個資料夾，裡面一定要有 SKILL.md，frontmatter 至少要有 name（最多 64 字元，小寫英數與連字號，且要和資料夾同名）與 description（最多 1024 字元）。另外可以放 scripts/、references/、assets/。agent 啟動時只讀每個 skill 的名稱與描述，任務對上了才載入完整內容，需要時再讀附帶檔案或執行腳本。

二、還沒說清楚的地方

  • 沒有時間表。版本化發布、提案流程、安全指引都還在「提議」階段，公告沒有給日期。
  • 「支援」的程度不一樣。70 多個平台整合，不代表每個平台的行為都相同。規格裡的 allowed-tools（預先核准 skill 可以用哪些工具）本身就標註為實驗性質，各家實作可能不同。
  • 安全指引還沒出來。skill 可以附帶可執行的腳本，而安裝量已經是億級。在正式指引出來之前，怎麼審查、怎麼發布，目前還是各團隊自己負責。
  • 數字是單方說法。100 萬、2.8 億這類數字來自 Anthropic，沒有第三方統計可以對照。

三、我怎麼解讀

skill 從「某家工具的設定」變成「團隊的資產」

以前寫給某個 agent 的指令檔，很容易被當成個人設定：放在自己的家目錄、換工具就重寫。標準交給中立組織之後，比較能放心地把 skill 當成團隊共用、跟著 repo 走的東西。這跟當年大家開始把 CI 設定、lint 規則放進版本控制是同一個轉變。

真正的價值在「做法」，不在格式

skill 的格式很簡單，難的是內容：你們團隊怎麼發版、怎麼 review、出事時先查哪裡。這些過去散在 wiki、資深同事的腦袋和 Slack 討論裡。agent 能不能做對事，很大程度取決於這些做法有沒有被寫清楚。標準化解決的是「寫一次到處用」，沒有解決「寫什麼」。

skill 也是供應鏈的一部分

一個 skill 可以帶 Bash 或 Python 腳本，agent 會照著說明去執行。從風險角度看，安裝一個來路不明的 skill，跟 npm install 一個沒看過的套件很像，甚至更直接，因為執行它的是一個會自己做決定的 agent。

四、團隊開始累積 skills 前的檢查清單

  1. 放進版本控制。團隊共用的 skill 跟著 repo 或獨立的 skills repo 走，修改要經過 PR review，不要散在各人電腦裡。
  2. 外部 skill 先讀再裝。特別是 scripts/ 裡的東西。來源不明的 skill，先在沙箱或沒有正式憑證的環境試。
  3. description 要寫準。agent 是靠 description 判斷要不要啟用 skill，寫得太泛會被誤觸發，寫得太窄則永遠用不到。規格建議同時寫「做什麼」和「什麼時候用」。
  4. 一個 skill 只做一件事。規格建議 SKILL.md 控制在 500 行以內，細節拆到 references/。一個萬用 skill 很難維護，也很難審查。
  5. 不要依賴實驗性欄位做權限控管。allowed-tools 還是實驗性質，真正的權限邊界應該設在 agent 平台、沙箱與憑證本身。
  6. 可以用官方工具驗證格式。規格提供 skills-ref validate 檢查 frontmatter 與命名，適合放進 CI。
  7. 追蹤 AAIF 的安全指引。指引出來後，回頭檢查既有的 skills 與安裝流程。

五、跟我自己的做法

這個網站的 repo 裡就放了不少 agent skills，用來跑規劃、開發、審查的流程。我的經驗是，skill 寫得好不好，差別幾乎都在「有沒有把隱性的判斷寫出來」：什麼情況該停下來問人、什麼情況可以直接做。這也是導入 agent 時最值得花時間的地方：先把人的做法講清楚，再交給機器執行。

如果你在意的是 agent 能連到哪些外部系統，可以參考我前一篇談 Copilot connectors 與 MCP 治理；skills 管的是 agent 會怎麼做事，兩者要一起看。

Skills 標準化之後，「寫一次、多個 agent 共用」變得可行，但寫什麼、誰能改、外部的能不能信，還是團隊自己要決定的事。如果你想替團隊整理第一批 skills、或規劃 agent 的導入流程，可以預約 30 分鐘初談。

title: The year-end EOL calendar: .NET 8/9 and PostgreSQL 14 expire next week, Python 3.10 is already gone
summary: .NET 8 and 9 reach end of support on November 10 and PostgreSQL 14 on November 12. Python 3.10 and Kubernetes 1.34 already expired in October, and PHP 8.2 follows on December 31. Official dates, what EOL actually costs, inventory commands, and the upgrade targets I recommend.
html:
The year-end EOL calendar

Q4 is always heavy on end-of-life dates, and this year they cluster tightly. .NET 8 and .NET 9 both reach end of support on November 10, and the final PostgreSQL 14 release is scheduled for November 12. Looking back, Python 3.10 stopped receiving support after its last release on October 1, and Kubernetes 1.34 expired on October 27.

EOL doesn't break anything on the day itself, which is exactly why it keeps getting pushed back. This post puts the dates in one place and explains why I don't think this round should be postponed.

1. The dates

ComponentEnd of supportUpgrade target
Python 3.102026-10-01 (final release 3.10.22)3.12 or 3.13
Kubernetes 1.342026-10-271.35 or later, on your provider's schedule
.NET 8 (LTS), .NET 9 (STS)2026-11-10.NET 10 (LTS, supported until November 2028)
PostgreSQL 142026-11-1217 or 18
PHP 8.22026-12-318.4 or 8.5

A few details:

  • .NET 9 is an STS release, but Microsoft now supports STS for 24 months, so it ends on the same day as .NET 8. The policy page notes that end dates line up with Patch Tuesday, the second Tuesday of the month.
  • The last PostgreSQL 14 release ships with the regular update on 11/12. PostgreSQL 19 RC2 lands the same day, with GA planned for 11/19, though the project says that date can slip.
  • PEP 619 now lists Python 3.10 as end-of-life: the branch is frozen and accepts no further changes.
  • The PHP 8.2 date comes from php.net's 8.2.35 announcement.

2. The cost of EOL showed up this month

The clearest example is PHP last month. On October 21 the project fixed two exploited remote code execution bugs (details in this post). Every branch from 8.2 up got a release; 8.1 and older got nothing from upstream, leaving only distro or LTS-vendor backports.

That's what EOL really means. Everything is fine until the day something breaks, and then "bump the patch version" is no longer an option. You're left with an emergency major upgrade or finding someone to backport for you, and a major upgrade is the last thing you want to do under attack.

Two distinctions worth keeping in mind:

  • Upstream EOL is not distro EOL. Python or PostgreSQL installed from Ubuntu or RHEL packages may still get fixes from the distro, depending on its policy.
  • Managed services run their own schedules. Managed databases and managed Kubernetes often offer extended support, sometimes for an extra fee. I haven't checked every provider's policy, so go by your provider's notices.

3. How to take inventory

These are common commands; I haven't run them in your environment:

# Runtimes
python3 --version
dotnet --list-runtimes
php -v
kubectl version          # look at Server Version
psql -c 'SHOW server_version;'

# Versions pinned in your projects
grep -rn '<TargetFramework' --include='*.csproj' .
grep -rnE 'python-version|dotnet-version|php-version' .github/workflows/

# Base images used by your Dockerfiles
grep -rhE '^FROM ' --include='Dockerfile*' . | sort | uniq -c

What usually gets missed: CI runners, scheduled jobs, internal tools, and "that small service a colleague built three years ago." Production tends to have an owner. These don't.

4. Upgrade notes

  • .NET 8/9 to 10: five days left. If you can't do everything, start with internet-facing services. Change TargetFramework, update packages, run the tests; this is usually the simplest of the bunch.
  • PostgreSQL 14 to 17 or 18: use pg_upgrade or dump and restore. I wouldn't move production to 19 the week it ships; wait for the first minor release or two. Going from 14 to 18 already gets you most of the benefit. Rehearse on a replica first and measure the downtime.
  • Python 3.10 to 3.12/3.13: check your dependencies' supported versions first. Once the interpreter stops getting fixes, libraries drop 3.10 too, and eventually you can't install their security updates either.
  • Kubernetes 1.34: on managed clusters, follow your provider's timeline, but don't wait for a forced upgrade. Upgrading yourself at least lets you pick the time.
  • PHP 8.2: under two months to go. Next sprint is a good slot.

5. Checklist

  • Run the inventory across production, CI, container images and internal tools
  • Handle internet-facing .NET 8/9 services this week
  • Set a date for the PostgreSQL 14 upgrade and rehearse it on a replica
  • Check your managed providers' extended-support terms and pricing
  • Schedule Python 3.10 and PHP 8.2 into the next two sprints
  • Pin versions in your repos (.python-version, global.json, engines) so they can be checked automatically
  • Put every component's EOL date on the team calendar with a reminder one quarter ahead

I've long thought EOL management is one of the highest-return habits in operations. The dates are published years in advance and can be scheduled like anything else, yet they're routinely left until something goes wrong. If you want version inventory and upgrades on a regular cadence, book a 30-minute intro call.

title: 年底 EOL 行事曆：.NET 8／9、PostgreSQL 14 下週到期，Python 3.10 已經停止支援
summary: .NET 8 與 9 在 11/10、PostgreSQL 14 在 11/12 結束支援，Python 3.10 與 Kubernetes 1.34 在 10 月已經到期，PHP 8.2 則是 12/31。整理官方日期、EOL 的實際代價、盤點指令，以及我建議的升級目標。
html:
年底 EOL 行事曆

每年第四季都是 EOL 的高峰，今年特別集中：.NET 8 與 .NET 9 在 11 月 10 日同一天結束支援，PostgreSQL 14 的最後一次更新排在 11 月 12 日。往回看，Python 3.10 在 10 月 1 日發布最後一版後已經停止支援，Kubernetes 1.34 也在 10 月 27 日到期。

EOL 不會讓服務當天就壞掉，所以很容易被一路往後推。這篇把日期整理在一起，順便說明為什麼我認為這次不該再推。

一、日期總表

元件結束支援我建議的升級目標
Python 3.102026-10-01（最後一版 3.10.22）3.12 或 3.13
Kubernetes 1.342026-10-271.35 以上，依雲端供應商排程
.NET 8（LTS）、.NET 9（STS）2026-11-10.NET 10（LTS，支援到 2028 年 11 月）
PostgreSQL 142026-11-1217 或 18
PHP 8.22026-12-318.4 或 8.5

幾個細節：

  • .NET 9 是 STS，但微軟已經把 STS 的支援期改成 24 個月，所以它和 .NET 8 同一天到期。官方說明結束日對齊每月第二個星期二的 Patch Tuesday。
  • PostgreSQL 14 的最後一版會和 11/12 的例行更新一起發布；同一天 PostgreSQL 19 釋出 RC2，正式版預計 11/19，但官方也說如果有問題可能延後。
  • Python 3.10 在 PEP 619 裡已經標示為 end-of-life，程式碼凍結，不再接受任何修正。
  • PHP 8.2 的日期來自 php.net 在 8.2.35 的公告。

二、EOL 的代價，這個月就看得到

最直接的例子是上個月的 PHP。10 月 21 日官方修補了兩個已遭利用的遠端程式碼執行漏洞（詳見這篇），8.2 以上都有新版，8.1 以前則官方不再修補，只能靠發行版或 LTS 廠商的 backport。

這就是 EOL 的真正意思：平常一切正常，等到真的出事那天，你沒有「升一個小版本」這個選項，只剩「緊急做一次大版本升級」或「找人幫你 backport」。而大版本升級最不適合在被攻擊的壓力下做。

另外要分清楚兩件事：

  • 上游 EOL 不等於發行版 EOL。透過 Ubuntu、RHEL 套件安裝的 Python 或 PostgreSQL，可能還有發行版的修補，要看各自的支援政策。
  • 託管服務有自己的時程。雲端的託管資料庫、託管 Kubernetes 常有延長支援，有些要另外收費。我沒有逐一確認各家的政策，請以你的供應商公告為準。

三、怎麼盤點

以下指令是常見寫法，我沒有在你的環境測過：

# 執行環境
python3 --version
dotnet --list-runtimes
php -v
kubectl version          # 看 Server Version
psql -c 'SHOW server_version;'

# 專案裡寫死的版本
grep -rn '<TargetFramework' --include='*.csproj' .
grep -rnE 'python-version|dotnet-version|php-version' .github/workflows/

# Dockerfile 用了哪些 base image
grep -rhE '^FROM ' --include='Dockerfile*' . | sort | uniq -c

盤點時最常漏掉的是 CI runner、排程任務、內部工具，以及「某個同事三年前做的小服務」。正式環境通常有人顧，這些沒有。

四、各項升級的建議

  • .NET 8／9 → 10：只剩五天，來不及全部升完就先處理對外的服務。改 TargetFramework、更新套件、跑完測試，通常是最單純的一個。
  • PostgreSQL 14 → 17 或 18：用 pg_upgrade 或 dump／restore。我不建議正式環境在 19 剛發布就直接跳過去，等第一、二個小版本再說；從 14 升到 18 已經能拿到大部分好處。升級前務必在複本上演練一次，量好停機時間。
  • Python 3.10 → 3.12／3.13：先確認相依套件的支援範圍。直譯器不再修補之後，相依套件也會陸續停止支援 3.10，到時連套件的安全更新都裝不上。
  • Kubernetes 1.34：託管叢集照供應商的升級時程走，但不要等它強制升級；自己升至少能選時間。
  • PHP 8.2：還有不到兩個月，現在排進下個 sprint 剛好。

五、清單

  • 用上面的指令盤點正式環境、CI、容器映像、內部工具的版本
  • 本週內處理對外的 .NET 8／9 服務
  • PostgreSQL 14 排定升級日期，先在複本上演練
  • 確認託管服務的延長支援政策與費用
  • Python 3.10、PHP 8.2 排進接下來兩個 sprint
  • 在專案裡固定版本（.python-version、global.json、engines），讓版本變成可檢查的規則
  • 把各元件的 EOL 日期寫進團隊行事曆，提前一季提醒

我一直認為，EOL 管理是維運裡投資報酬率最高的事之一：日期幾年前就公布了，完全可以預先排程，卻常常拖到出事才處理。如果你想把版本盤點和升級排成固定節奏，可以預約 30 分鐘初談。

title: Two months into EU CRA reporting: the 24-hour clock belongs in your outsourcing contract
summary: The EU Cyber Resilience Act's vulnerability and incident reporting duties have applied since September 11, and ENISA upgraded its Single Reporting Platform to version 1.3 on November 4. What's settled, what isn't, and what contract and outsourced projects should add to their agreements.
html:
Two months into EU CRA reporting

The reporting duties in Article 14 of the EU Cyber Resilience Act (CRA) have applied since September 11, 2026. The same day, ENISA launched the CRA Single Reporting Platform (SRP), and the SRP page notes it was upgraded to version 1.3 on November 4, with documentation still being brought up to date. The European Commission's CRA reporting page lays out the process and deadlines.

This isn't legal advice. What I want to look at is this: when your client sells a product into the EU and you (or your team) built it, how does that 24-hour clock land on the delivery process and the contract?

1. What's settled

From the Commission's page:

  • Who reports: manufacturers of products with digital elements.
  • What: actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe incidents affecting the product's security.
  • Deadlines: an early warning within 24 hours of becoming aware; a full notification within 72 hours; a final report within 14 days after a corrective measure is available for vulnerabilities, or within one month of the 72-hour notification for severe incidents.
  • How: report once through the SRP. It goes to the CSIRT where the manufacturer has its main establishment, and ENISA receives it at the same time.
  • Open-source stewards: their reporting duties don't apply until December 11, 2027.

Two law firm write-ups add a few points. Hogan Lovells' September 11 article and Jones Day's July alert both cite the Commission's guidance:

  • Products already on the EU market are covered, not only new ones.
  • Exploitation known before September 11 does not need to be reported retroactively.
  • "Becoming aware" means that, after an initial assessment, there is a reasonable degree of certainty that a vulnerability is being actively exploited or that a severe incident has compromised the product's security.
  • Manufacturers must inform impacted users and, where appropriate, all users (Article 14(8), per Hogan Lovells).
  • Jones Day notes fines of up to EUR 15 million or 2.5% of worldwide annual turnover, whichever is higher.

Most of the CRA's other requirements, including the security requirements for the products themselves, apply from December 11, 2027. Only reporting is live now.

2. What's unclear, or not covered here

  • Whether your product is in scope depends on what it is and how it's used, and I can't decide that for you. Pure SaaS, internal systems and device firmware are very different cases. Check with a lawyer who knows the CRA.
  • Who the "manufacturer" is gets blurry in outsourced work. My reading is that it's mainly the party placing the product on the market under its own name, usually the client rather than the contractor. That's my reading, not a legal conclusion.
  • I did not read the Commission's full July guidance directly. The points above on legacy products and awareness come from the two law firms' summaries.
  • The SRP documentation is still catching up with version 1.3, and Hogan Lovells notes that voluntary reporting (Article 15) wasn't in the launch version. Details may still change.

3. What it means for contract and outsourced work

The rule names the manufacturer. But answering "does this vulnerability affect our product, which versions, and is it being exploited?" within 24 hours depends on information the development team holds:

  • Which packages and versions does the product use?
  • Which version is deployed at which customer?
  • If the alert arrives at 2 a.m., who can assess the impact within a few hours?
  • How long until a fix ships?

If that lives only in a contractor's head, or nobody maintains the project after hand-off, the client's 24-hour clock runs straight into a wall. It's one reason I keep arguing that delivery should start from architecture and maintainability: things that can be handed over and traced are what help at moments like this.

It cuts the other way too. A delivery team that can write down exactly how it will respond when a vulnerability appears is a more convincing partner for clients selling into the EU.

4. What to add to contracts and delivery

  1. Make the component inventory a deliverable. Ship a list of dependencies and versions with every release, ideally as an SBOM (CycloneDX or SPDX), not just the source code.
  2. Set a vulnerability notification window. When the contractor finds or hears about a vulnerability, how many hours until the client's named contact is told? It has to be much shorter than 24 hours so the client has time to assess and report.
  3. Define the maintenance period and terms. Who handles security updates after hand-off, for how long, and how it's billed. My post on engagement models covers turning maintenance into a retainer.
  4. Keep versions and deployments traceable. Which version, which date, which environment, written down, not remembered.
  5. Agree on contacts and escalation. Primary and backup contacts on both sides, and how to reach someone outside office hours.
  6. Rehearse once a year. Take a real CVE through the whole flow: assess impact, notify, fix, release, and see how long it actually takes. Hogan Lovells also passes on ENISA's advice: have the responsible staff set up EU Login with multi-factor authentication now, and register as an Assigned Representative only when a report is actually needed.

Reporting is only the first step; fuller product requirements arrive at the end of 2027. Writing component inventories, notification windows and maintenance periods into contracts now costs little and makes a big difference when something happens. If you're planning a product for the EU market or want to add security delivery terms to an outsourcing contract, book a 30-minute intro call.

title: 歐盟 CRA 通報義務上路兩個月：24 小時的時鐘，外包合約要先寫清楚
summary: 歐盟 Cyber Resilience Act 的漏洞與事件通報義務從 9 月 11 日起適用，ENISA 的單一通報平台 11 月 4 日升級到 1.3 版。整理目前確定的規則、還沒說清楚的地方，以及接案與外包專案該在合約裡補上的幾件事。
html:
歐盟 CRA 通報義務上路兩個月

歐盟《網路韌性法》（Cyber Resilience Act，CRA）第 14 條的通報義務，從 2026 年 9 月 11 日起適用。同一天，ENISA 上線了 CRA Single Reporting Platform（SRP）；SRP 頁面也註明平台在 11 月 4 日升級到 1.3 版，相關文件仍在更新中。歐盟執委會的 CRA reporting 說明頁整理了通報流程與時限。

這篇不是法律意見。我想談的是：當你的客戶把產品賣進歐盟，而產品是你（或你的團隊）開發的，這個 24 小時的時鐘會怎麼落到交付流程和合約上。

一、目前確定的規則

依據執委會說明頁：

  • 誰要通報：「具數位元素產品」（products with digital elements）的製造商。
  • 通報什麼：正被主動利用的漏洞（actively exploited vulnerabilities），以及影響產品安全的嚴重事件。
  • 時限：知悉後 24 小時內提出早期預警；72 小時內提出完整通報；漏洞在修正措施可用後 14 天內交最終報告，嚴重事件則在 72 小時通報後一個月內交最終報告。
  • 怎麼通報：透過 SRP 通報一次，送到製造商主要營業據點所在國的 CSIRT，ENISA 同步收到。
  • 開源管理者（open-source software stewards）：通報義務從 2027 年 12 月 11 日才適用。

另外兩份律師事務所的整理補充了幾個重點。Hogan Lovells 在 9 月 11 日的文章與 Jones Day 在 7 月的 alert 都引用執委會的指引指出：

  • 已經在歐盟市場上的舊產品也適用，不是只有新上市的產品。
  • 9 月 11 日之前已知的漏洞利用不需要追溯通報。
  • 「知悉」指的是經初步評估後，有合理程度的確定性認為漏洞正被利用，或嚴重事件已經影響產品安全。
  • 製造商必須通知受影響的使用者，適當時通知所有使用者（Hogan Lovells 註明是第 14 條第 8 項）。
  • Jones Day 提到，違反規定的罰款上限為 1,500 萬歐元或全球年營業額 2.5%，取較高者。

CRA 其他大部分要求（包含產品本身的資安要求）要到 2027 年 12 月 11 日才全面適用。現在先上路的只有通報這一塊。

二、還沒說清楚、或這篇沒處理的地方

  • 你的產品在不在範圍內，要看產品型態與用途，這篇沒辦法替你判斷。純 SaaS、內部系統、硬體韌體的情況差很多，請找熟悉 CRA 的律師確認。
  • 「製造商」是誰，在外包情境特別容易模糊。我的理解是以「用自己名義把產品放上市場的一方」為主，通常是客戶而不是接案方，但這是我的讀法，不是法律結論。
  • 我沒有直接讀到執委會 7 月發布的完整指引，上面關於舊產品與「知悉」的說明來自兩家律師事務所的整理。
  • SRP 的文件還在跟著 1.3 版更新，Hogan Lovells 也提到自願通報（第 15 條）在上線版本還沒有。細節可能還會變。

三、對接案與外包的意義

規則寫的是製造商，但 24 小時內要回答「這個漏洞有沒有影響我們的產品、影響哪些版本、有沒有在被利用」，靠的是開發方的資訊：

  • 產品用了哪些套件、哪些版本？
  • 哪個版本部署在哪些客戶那裡？
  • 半夜接到通知，誰能在幾小時內判斷影響範圍？
  • 修正要多久才能出？

如果這些資訊只存在接案工程師的腦袋裡，或專案結案後就沒人維護，客戶的 24 小時時鐘會直接撞牆。這也是為什麼我一直主張交付要從架構和可維護性開始：能交接、能追蹤的東西，在這種時候才有用。

反過來說，對接案方這也是機會。能在合約裡清楚寫出「漏洞發生時我們怎麼配合」的團隊，對要賣進歐盟的客戶會更有說服力。

四、合約與交付該補上的清單

  1. **元件清單列為交付物。**每次正式發布都附上相依套件與版本清單（SBOM 格式最好，例如 CycloneDX 或 SPDX），而不是只交程式碼。
  2. **寫明漏洞通知時限。**接案方發現或收到漏洞資訊後，要在幾小時內通知客戶的指定窗口。這個時限必須比 24 小時短得多，客戶才有時間評估與通報。
  3. **定義維護期與維護方式。**結案後誰負責安全更新、持續多久、怎麼計費。可以參考我寫過的接案合作模式，把維護做成 retainer。
  4. **版本與部署紀錄要能追溯。**哪個版本、哪一天、部署到哪個環境，要有紀錄，不能只靠記憶。
  5. **約定聯絡窗口與升級路徑。**雙方各留主要與備援聯絡人，寫清楚非上班時間怎麼找到人。
  6. **一年做一次演練。**拿一個真實的 CVE 走一次流程：判斷影響、通知、修正、出版本，看看實際要花多久。另外，Hogan Lovells 引述 ENISA 的建議：負責人員先設好 EU Login 與多因素驗證，真的需要通報時再註冊為 Assigned Representative。

CRA 的通報義務只是第一步，2027 年底還有更完整的產品要求。現在把元件清單、通知時限和維護期寫進合約，成本不高，事情發生時卻差很多。如果你正在規劃要賣進歐盟的產品，或想替外包合約補上資安交付條款，歡迎預約 30 分鐘初談。

title: GitHub Enterprise now includes Copilot: no seat charge, but usage is billed from the first request
summary: On October 28, GitHub introduced a billing model called Copilot access: users with a GitHub Enterprise Cloud license pay no Copilot seat charge, but there is no included allowance, so usage is billed from the first request. The rules, what keeps working without budget, and the math to do before deciding whether to switch.
html:
GitHub Enterprise now includes Copilot: no seat charge, usage billed from the first request

On October 28, GitHub announced in its changelog that GitHub Enterprise now includes access to GitHub Copilot, and the official docs describe the new model, called "Copilot access." The headline reads like "Copilot is now free." What actually changes is the billing logic: from per head to per use.

For teams already on Copilot, and especially those letting agents do code review or run tasks in the cloud, this changes how the budget is built and who owns it.

1. The rules

Based on the changelog and the docs:

  1. Seat charge. Users with a GitHub Enterprise Cloud (GHEC) license have a $0 Copilot seat charge. Users without one can get Copilot Standalone at $10 per user per month.
  2. No included allowance. Usage is metered from the first request against the enterprise budget. For comparison, Copilot Business is $19 per user per month with 1,900 AI credits, and Copilot Enterprise is $39 with 3,900 AI credits, both pooled across the enterprise.
  3. Same features as Copilot Enterprise. Feature and model eligibility match Copilot Enterprise, subject to admin policies and spending controls.
  4. An empty budget does not cut people off. Code completion and next edit suggestions keep working without budget. Copilot Chat, Copilot code review and Copilot in the cloud need available budget. The changelog says an exhausted budget "never removes access"; the seat stays.
  5. No mixing. One enterprise cannot combine Copilot access with Business or Enterprise seats, not even by splitting them across organizations. GHEC users and Standalone users can coexist.
  6. No automatic rollout. Enterprise owners still have to assign seats to members, teams or organizations, including people who already hold a GHEC license.

Eligibility is narrow for now: enterprises that work with a GitHub or Microsoft account team can sign up from October 28. Self-serve customers cannot yet; GitHub says access will open in stages, with dates shared "in the coming weeks." GitHub Free, Team and self-service GHEC trials are not eligible. Transitions take effect on the first day of a month, and Copilot Business and Enterprise remain on sale, so nothing changes if you do not opt in.

2. What is not spelled out

  • The unit price lives elsewhere. Neither the changelog nor this docs page says what an AI credit costs; they point to the models and pricing reference. To do the math you need those per-model rates.
  • The budget amount is yours to set. GitHub gives no recommended figure and no default cap.
  • No date for self-serve. Smaller teams usually buy self-serve, so for now they wait.

3. How I read it

Copilot cost now tracks agent work, not headcount

Budgeting for Copilot used to be simple: seats times price. In the new model the light features such as completions work without budget, and the spend comes from Chat, code review and cloud agents. In other words, cost grows with how much work you hand to agents. Once a team sends every PR through Copilot code review and lets cloud agents pick up issues, the cost curve moves with it.

Whether it pays off depends on usage

  • Many people who mostly use completions and occasionally ask Chat: dropping the seat charge will likely save money.
  • A smaller group of heavy users running lots of agent work: the pooled credits in Business or Enterprise used to absorb part of that. Under Copilot access, all of it is billed from the first request, so the switch may not pay.

GitHub's docs recommend estimating first: add up current license and overage charges, estimate the cost of all usage with no included allowance, add Standalone users times $10, and compare the two totals.

The budget becomes a governance control

"An empty budget does not cut access, but Chat, code review and cloud agents stop" effectively turns the budget into a switch: the amount you set decides how much work agents can do each month. That is not just a finance call. It is an engineering management decision.

4. Checklist before evaluating or switching

  1. Pull your current usage. Use the Copilot usage metrics API to see actual usage, broken down by user, client and model. On November 3, GitHub started breaking out BYOK and enterprise custom model usage, so watch which usage does not actually flow through GitHub billing.
  2. Follow the official estimation steps, paying particular attention to the usage your pooled credits currently absorb. After a switch, all of it becomes real spend.
  3. Leave room for growth. If you plan to widen agent use next year, today's usage is not your ceiling.
  4. Keep the AI credits paid usage policy enabled in AI Controls. The docs say it is on by default; if it is turned off, users cannot use features that consume credits.
  5. Check your firewall allowlist. Copilot access uses the Copilot Enterprise endpoint. If your allowlist only has *.business.githubcopilot.com, add *.enterprise.githubcopilot.com.
  6. Manage models alongside the budget. The Copilot model policy API went GA on October 19, letting you control available models at the enterprise, team and organization levels. Who gets the expensive models shows up directly on the bill.
  7. Confirm the effective date with your account team. Transitions start on the first of a month, so align it with your billing and internal budget cycles.

5. Advice for smaller teams

Most of the smaller teams I work with buy Copilot Business self-serve, so this model is not available to them yet. The direction is clear, though: AI developer tools are moving from buying seats to buying usage. Rather than waiting for self-serve access to do the math, start on two things now: know which work each team actually hands to agents, and what that work is worth.

It ties back to my post on how AI agents produce more code but not more software: more agent activity does not mean more delivery. Usage-based billing puts that gap straight onto the invoice.

A $0 seat is good news, but no allowance and billing from the first request means AI spend now needs to be managed the way cloud spend is. If you want help estimating your team's Copilot usage and budget, or deciding which work is worth handing to agents, book a 30-minute intro call.

title: GitHub Enterprise 內含 Copilot：席位費歸零，但從第一個請求開始計費
summary: GitHub 10 月 28 日推出「Copilot access」計費模式：有 GitHub Enterprise Cloud 授權的人不再付 Copilot 席位費，但也沒有內含額度，用量從第一個請求就計費。整理規則、哪些功能沒預算也能用，以及評估要不要轉換時該算的帳。
html:
GitHub Enterprise 內含 Copilot：席位費歸零，用量從第一個請求開始算

10 月 28 日，GitHub 在 changelog 宣布 GitHub Enterprise 現在可以內含 Copilot，並在官方文件說明這個叫「Copilot access」的新模式。標題看起來像「Copilot 免費送」，但實際上是計費邏輯從按人頭轉成按用量。

對已經在用 Copilot、而且開始讓 agent 做 code review、在雲端跑任務的團隊來說，這會直接影響預算怎麼編、誰來管。

一、規則是什麼

依 changelog 與官方文件：

  1. 席位費：有 GitHub Enterprise Cloud（GHEC）授權的使用者，Copilot 席位費是 0；沒有 GHEC 授權的人可以用 Copilot Standalone，每人每月 10 美元。
  2. 沒有內含額度：用量從第一個請求開始，計入企業預算。對照之下，Copilot Business 是每人每月 19 美元、含 1,900 AI credits；Copilot Enterprise 是 39 美元、含 3,900 AI credits，兩者的額度都在企業內共用。
  3. 功能等同 Copilot Enterprise：可用的功能與模型和 Copilot Enterprise 相同，再依管理者的政策與支出控制限制。
  4. 預算用完不會斷線：code completion 與 next edit suggestions 在沒有預算時仍可使用；Copilot Chat、Copilot code review、Copilot in the cloud 則需要有可用預算。changelog 的原話是預算耗盡「never removes access」，席位本身不會被拿掉。
  5. 不能混用：同一個 enterprise 不能同時有 Copilot access 和 Business／Enterprise 席位，連在不同 organization 分開也不行。但 GHEC 使用者和 Standalone 使用者可以並存。
  6. 不會自動開通：enterprise owner 仍要把席位指派給成員、團隊或 organization，包括原本就有 GHEC 授權的人。

適用對象目前有限：有 GitHub 或 Microsoft 業務窗口的企業，從 10 月 28 日起可以申請。自助購買的客戶還不能用，GitHub 說會分階段開放、日期「in the coming weeks」公布；GitHub Free、Team 與 GHEC 自助試用則不適用。轉換從每月 1 日生效，Copilot Business 與 Enterprise 也照常販售，不轉換就不受影響。

二、沒說清楚的地方

  • 單價要另外查。changelog 與這份說明文件都沒有寫每個 AI credit 多少錢，只指向模型與價格的參考頁。要算帳，得把各模型的費率一起拿來看。
  • 「預算」的金額由你決定。GitHub 沒有給建議值，也沒有預設上限，這件事完全落在企業自己身上。
  • 自助客戶的時程未定。中小團隊多半是自助購買，目前只能等。

三、我怎麼解讀

Copilot 的成本開始跟著 agent 走，而不是跟著人頭走

過去編 Copilot 預算很簡單：人數乘以單價。新模式下，補全這類輕量功能沒預算也能用，真正要花錢的是 Chat、code review、雲端 agent。也就是說，成本會跟著「讓 agent 做多少事」成長。一個團隊開始把每個 PR 都丟給 Copilot code review、讓雲端 agent 處理 issue，費用曲線就會跟著變。

誰划算、誰不划算，取決於用法

  • 很多人只用補全、偶爾問 Chat：席位費省下來，很可能比較便宜。
  • 少數重度使用者大量跑 agent：原本 Business／Enterprise 的共用額度可以吸收一部分，轉過去之後全部從第一個請求計費，就不一定划算。

官方文件也是建議先估算：把目前的授權費與超額用量加總，再估算「沒有內含額度時」全部用量的成本，加上 Standalone 人數乘以 10 美元，最後兩邊比較。

預算變成治理工具

「預算耗盡不斷線，但 Chat、code review、雲端 agent 會停」這個設計，等於把預算變成一個開關：設多少，就決定了 agent 每個月能做多少事。這不只是財務問題，也是工程管理的決策。

四、評估與轉換前的檢查清單

  1. 先拉出目前的用量。用 Copilot usage metrics API 看實際用量（可以依使用者、用戶端、模型拆開看）；GitHub 11 月 3 日也把 BYOK 與企業自訂模型的用量分開列出，算帳時要注意哪些用量其實不走 GitHub 計費。
  2. 照官方步驟估算，特別是「目前被共用額度吸收掉的那部分」，轉換後都會變成實際支出。
  3. 設預算時預留成長。如果明年打算擴大 agent 的使用範圍，現在的用量不能直接當上限。
  4. 確認 AI Controls 裡的 AI credits paid usage policy 維持開啟。文件說這個政策預設開啟，關掉的話，使用者就無法使用需要 credits 的功能。
  5. 檢查防火牆白名單。Copilot access 走的是 Copilot Enterprise 的端點，如果白名單只有 *.business.githubcopilot.com，要加上 *.enterprise.githubcopilot.com。
  6. 搭配模型政策一起管。Copilot 模型政策 API 已在 10 月 19 日 GA，可以在 enterprise、團隊、organization 層級控制可用模型。貴的模型開給誰，直接影響每月帳單。
  7. 跟業務窗口確認生效日。轉換從每月 1 日生效，帳單週期與內部預算週期最好對齊。

五、給台灣團隊的建議

我接觸到的台灣中小團隊，多半是自助購買 Copilot Business，這次的模式暫時還用不到。但方向很清楚：AI 開發工具的計費正在從「買席位」轉向「買用量」。與其等到自助開放才算帳，不如現在就開始做兩件事：知道每個團隊實際把哪些工作交給了 agent，以及這些工作值多少錢。

這也呼應我在AI agent 產出更多程式碼，不等於更多軟體裡的觀點：agent 跑得多，不代表交付得多。用量計費會讓這個落差直接出現在帳單上。

席位費歸零是好消息，但沒有額度、從第一個請求開始算，代表 AI 成本要像雲端成本一樣被管理。如果你想替團隊估算 Copilot 的用量與預算，或規劃哪些工作值得交給 agent，可以預約 30 分鐘初談。

title: The Next.js November security release: this time it is about cache identity, not RCE
summary: On November 3, Next.js shipped 16.4.5 and 15.5.29 with fixes for seven issues, most of them about how Cache Components derives cache keys and isolates tenants. Which code patterns are affected, which deployments matter, and the habits worth building if you use use cache in a multi-tenant app.
html:
The Next.js November security release

Next.js posted an advance notice on October 27 and shipped the November 2026 Security Release on November 3. The patched versions are 16.4.5 (Active LTS) and 15.5.29 (Maintenance LTS).

Compared with October's two Critical RCEs (covered in Next.js 16.4 and the October security update), this one looks mild. After reading it closely, I think it deserves more attention from people who make architecture decisions, not less: four of the seven issues come down to "the cache handed A's result to B." That is not one bug. It is a class of risk that comes with the Cache Components model itself.

1. What was announced

According to the release post, the seven issues are:

IssueSeverityPreconditions
Cross-tenant cache disclosure when mixing unstable_cache and use cacheHighCache Components enabled; the same use cache function is called both directly and inside unstable_cache, and it reads a root parameter such as a tenant ID
Cross-root-parameter disclosure in nested use cacheMediumAn inner cached function reads a root parameter and returns an early value plus a slower async value, and the outer function finishes without waiting
Cache identity collisions from binary argumentsMediumSecurity-relevant binary data (used to tell users apart, for example) is passed as a use cache argument
Shared shell cache poisoning when self-hostingMediumnext start, Cache Components on, Partial Prefetching off or unset, and a specific route shape
Cross-client response injection via stale compressed framingMediumSelf-hosted, returning an attacker-controlled fetched Response unchanged, behind an HTTP/1.1 reverse proxy that queues pipelined requests on a shared connection
Cookie values exposed through an internal header in Edge routesMediumEdge Route Handlers or Pages Router Edge API routes setting a sensitive cookie with NextResponse.cookies.set(), plus attacker-controlled same-origin JavaScript
SVG rejection bypass in Image OptimizationMediumAn image from an allowed source is misclassified as AVIF and the image backend can decode SVG

For the High-severity issue, the advisory gives a complete workaround: do not call a use cache function inside unstable_cache().

2. What was unclear, or left for you to judge

  • The advance notice said "seven medium vulnerabilities"; the release lists one as High. The two posts disagree, and the release post is the one to trust. Treat advance notices as scheduling input, not as a severity assessment.
  • Nothing says whether deployments on Vercel are shielded at the platform level. Some issues are explicitly scoped to self-hosting; the rest are not. Do not assume you are fine just because you deploy to Vercel.
  • The Edge cookie issue needs attacker-controlled same-origin JavaScript, and the post is clear that it is not a standalone XSS vector. If your site loads third-party scripts, though, that precondition is less far-fetched than it sounds.
  • Only the 16.4 and 15.5 lines are patched. Projects on older versions have nothing to install this time.

3. What it means for technology choices

Cache Components and use cache make caching very easy to write: one directive and the function result is cached. The trade-off is that what makes up the cache key moves from explicit to implicit. When you built Redis keys by hand, you naturally included the tenant ID. Now the framework derives cache identity from arguments, root parameters and closures. It gets that right most of the time, and several of these issues sit exactly on the edges where the derivation went wrong.

My read is not that Cache Components is unsafe to use. It is that in a multi-tenant system, tenant isolation stays your responsibility and should not be delegated entirely to the framework. The framework will fix its bugs; your system should still avoid leaking data during the weeks before it does.

The other signal is the gap between platforms and self-hosting. Two of these issues only occur under next start or with particular reverse-proxy setups. If you self-host or use something like OpenNext, "are framework security fixes fully exercised in my environment?" belongs on your evaluation list.

4. Practical advice

  1. Upgrade first. 16.x goes to 16.4.5 and 15.5 goes to 15.5.29. Both are patch-level changes.

    pnpm add next@16.4.5   # 16.x
pnpm add next@15.5.29  # projects still on 15.5

  2. Search the codebase for unstable_cache. Mixing it with use cache is the precondition for the High issue. Use this release as the reason to retire the old API instead of keeping both.

  3. Review what your cached functions take as arguments. Pass values that identify users or accounts as strings or explicit IDs, not as Uint8Array or other binary data.

  4. Add a second check in multi-tenant apps. Before returning cached data, confirm its tenant ID matches the request. It costs very little and catches framework-level mistakes.

  5. If you self-host, look at your reverse proxy. If it does HTTP/1.1 pipelining onto shared backend connections, decide whether that needs changing, and check for routes that pass an external fetch Response straight through.

  6. If an Edge route sets sensitive cookies, send a real request after upgrading and check whether x-middleware-set-cookie still shows up. Where you can, the leak as reproduced did not affect Node.js Route Handlers or cookies set through cookies().set().

5. What it means for this site

8plus was on Next.js 16.4.1 with no Cache Components, no use cache and no Edge-runtime route handlers, so the caching issues do not apply here. It does use next/image, and the Vercel fallback runs real Next.js, so on November 5 it was bumped to 16.4.5 anyway (a patch upgrade; typecheck and the build needed no changes).

Production runs on Cloudflare Workers through vinext, which is a separate reimplementation of the Next.js APIs. These advisories are written against the next package, so I cannot infer whether vinext is affected; I will follow vinext's own announcements. That is a hidden cost of alternative runtimes: you now read two sets of security advisories.

Cache bugs are unpleasant because they rarely throw an error; they quietly hand data to the wrong person. The fix shipped quickly, but the lasting protection comes from your own design: cache keys you can explain, and a second check at tenant boundaries. If you are building a multi-tenant system on Cache Components and want a second pair of eyes on the caching and isolation design, book a 30-minute intro call.

title: Next.js 11 月安全更新：這次的重點是快取身分，不是 RCE
summary: 11/3 Next.js 發布 16.4.5 與 15.5.29，修補七個問題，其中多數跟 Cache Components 的快取鍵與多租戶隔離有關。整理哪些寫法會中、哪些部署方式才受影響，以及用 use cache 做多租戶時該建立的習慣。
html:
Next.js 11 月安全更新

10 月 27 日，Next.js 先發了預告，11 月 3 日正式發布 November 2026 Security Release：修補版本是 16.4.5（Active LTS）與 15.5.29（Maintenance LTS）。

跟 10 月那次兩個 Critical RCE 比起來（我在 Next.js 16.4 與 10 月安全更新 整理過），這次看起來溫和很多。但仔細讀完，我反而覺得這次更值得架構層面的人看：七個問題裡有四個跟「快取把 A 的結果給了 B」有關。 這不是單一 bug，而是 Cache Components 這種快取模型本身要面對的風險類型。

一、官方公布了什麼

依官方文章，七個問題如下：

問題等級前提條件
unstable_cache 與 use cache 混用時的跨租戶快取外洩High啟用 Cache Components，同一個 use cache 函式同時被直接呼叫、也在 unstable_cache 裡被呼叫，且函式讀取 root parameter（例如租戶 ID）
巢狀 use cache 的跨 root parameter 外洩Medium內層快取函式讀 root parameter，同時回傳一個先到的值與一個較慢的非同步值，外層沒等它就結束
二進位參數造成的快取身分碰撞Medium把具安全意義的二進位資料（例如用來區分使用者）當 use cache 參數
自架環境的共用 shell 快取污染Mediumnext start 自架、啟用 Cache Components、未啟用 Partial Prefetching，且路由結構符合特定條件
壓縮回應 framing 錯置造成的跨用戶回應注入Medium自架、原封不動回傳攻擊者可控的 fetch Response，前面有會在共用連線排隊 pipelined 請求的 HTTP/1.1 反向代理
Edge 路由的 cookie 值經內部 header 外洩MediumEdge Route Handler 或 Pages Router Edge API route 用 NextResponse.cookies.set() 設定敏感 cookie，且同源有攻擊者可控的 JavaScript
Image Optimization 的 SVG 拒絕機制被繞過Medium允許來源的圖片被誤判成 AVIF，而影像後端能解碼 SVG

第一個 High 等級的問題，advisory 寫明有完整的替代做法：不要在 unstable_cache() 裡呼叫 use cache 函式。

二、沒說清楚、或要自己判斷的地方

  • 預告寫的是「七個 medium」，正式公告卻有一個標成 High。 兩篇文章的說法不一致，以正式公告為準。這也提醒我們：預告只能拿來排時程，不能拿來判斷嚴重度。
  • 官方沒有說明 Vercel 平台上的部署是否因平台層而免疫。 有幾個問題明確寫了「self-hosted」，其他的沒寫，就不要自己假設在 Vercel 上就沒事。
  • Edge cookie 問題要搭配同源惡意 JavaScript 才成立，官方也強調它不是獨立的 XSS 管道。但如果你的站有第三方 script，這個前提沒有想像中遙遠。
  • 只修 16.4 與 15.5 兩條線。 還在更舊版本的專案，這次沒有修補可裝。

三、這對選型代表什麼

Cache Components 與 use cache 的設計讓快取變得很好寫：一個指令，函式結果就被快取。問題在於**「快取鍵由哪些東西組成」從顯性變成隱性**。過去你手寫 Redis key，會很自然地把 tenant ID 串進去；現在快取身分由框架從參數、root parameter、閉包推導，大多數時候是對的，但這次的幾個問題正好都發生在推導出錯的邊界上。

我的判斷是：這不代表 Cache Components 不能用，而是多租戶系統用它時，要把租戶隔離當成自己的責任，不要完全交給框架。框架會修 bug，但你的系統要在框架出 bug 的那幾週也不外洩資料。

另一個訊號是自架與平台的差距。這次有兩個問題只發生在 next start 自架、或特定反向代理配置下。選擇自架或 OpenNext 一類方案時，「框架的安全修補在你的環境上是否被完整測過」應該是評估項目之一。

四、實務建議

  1. 先升版。 16.x 升到 16.4.5、15.5 升到 15.5.29，都是 patch 等級。

    pnpm add next@16.4.5   # 16.x
pnpm add next@15.5.29  # 仍在 15.5 的專案

  2. 全專案搜一次 unstable_cache。 它跟 use cache 混用正是 High 等級問題的前提。趁這次把舊 API 收斂掉，不要兩套並存。

  3. 檢查快取函式的參數。 用來區分使用者或帳號的值，盡量以字串或明確的 ID 傳入，不要用 Uint8Array 之類的二進位資料當身分依據。

  4. 多租戶應用加一道防線。 從快取取出的資料，在回應前比對一次 tenant ID 是否一致。成本很低，卻能把框架層的錯誤擋在外面。

  5. 自架的團隊檢查反向代理。 如果前面是會做 HTTP/1.1 pipelining 的代理，評估一下是否需要調整；同時盤點有沒有路由把外部 fetch 的 Response 原樣回傳。

  6. Edge 路由有設敏感 cookie 的，升版後實際打一次請求，看回應 header 裡還有沒有 x-middleware-set-cookie。 能改用 Node.js runtime 或 cookies().set() 的，官方重現的外洩情境並不包含這兩種寫法。

五、對這個站的影響

8plus 原本是 Next.js 16.4.1，沒有啟用 Cache Components、沒有 use cache、也沒有 Edge runtime 的 route handler，所以前幾個快取問題對這個站不成立。但它有用 next/image，Vercel 備援環境跑的是正版 Next.js，所以 11/5 還是升到了 16.4.5（patch 升級，typecheck 與建置都沒有任何需要改的地方）。

正式環境透過 vinext 跑在 Cloudflare Workers 上。vinext 是重新實作 Next.js API 的另一套程式，這些 advisory 是針對 next 套件寫的，不能直接推論 vinext 受不受影響，我會另外追 vinext 那邊的公告。這也是用替代 runtime 時的隱性成本：安全公告要看兩份。

快取 bug 的麻煩在於它通常不會報錯，只會安靜地把資料給錯人。這次的修補很快，但更長久的保護來自你自己的設計：快取鍵要能說清楚、租戶邊界要有第二道檢查。如果你正在用 Cache Components 做多租戶系統，想一起檢視快取與隔離的設計，可以預約 30 分鐘初談。

title: Two exploited 9.2 PHP RCEs and a WordPress core flaw in KEV: what to do this week if you still run PHP
summary: PHP patched two unauthenticated remote code execution bugs on October 21, and CISA added both to its exploited list on October 26. The upgrade-process RCE fixed in WordPress 7.1.4 joined KEV on November 3. Here is who is affected, how to check, what is still unclear, and a checklist you can work through.
html:
Two weeks of PHP and WordPress in KEV

On October 21 the PHP project published an urgent security advisory for two unauthenticated remote code execution bugs, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, both rated 9.2 under CVSS v4.0. Five days later CISA added both to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, which means they are being used in real attacks. On October 28 WordPress shipped 7.1.4, and the upgrade-process RCE it fixes (CVE-2026-119977) landed in KEV on November 3.

A lot of teams will say "we're not a PHP shop." What I keep seeing with clients is a product written in Node or Go, next to a marketing site or blog on WordPress, or an early Laravel admin panel and a phpMyAdmin that nobody turned off. The box most likely to get you is the one everyone forgot was running.

1. What happened

PHP itself (Oct 20–26)

  • On 10/20 the project gave advance notice of a release at 14:00 UTC the next day, with both bugs rated CVSS v4.0 9.2.
  • On 10/21 it released 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35. One bug is state corruption when out-of-memory handling interrupts a request; the other is internal request state that outlives its memory and gets reused by the next request on the same worker.
  • According to the advisory, every PHP installation serving web requests is affected: PHP-FPM, Apache mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP and LiteSpeed. mod_php carries the highest risk.
  • PHP 8.1 and older get no fixes from the project. The security team pushed minimal source backport branches for 7.4, 8.0 and 8.1 to php-src, but whether you can use them depends on your distribution or LTS vendor.
  • On 10/23 an informational follow-up recommended disabling session.upload_progress until the next regular release, and said a full advisory for CVE-2026-115560 will ship with that release.
  • On 10/26 CISA added both CVEs to KEV.

WordPress core (Oct 28 – Nov 3)

  • 7.1.4 fixes 12 security issues. Most are stored XSS; the serious one is an "upgrade process weakness" that can lead to remote code execution during the upgrade window. The same release updates the bundled root certificates because of the eMudhra intermediate CA incident.
  • The NVD record, submitted by Wordfence, says versions 4.7 through 7.1.3 are affected because full-package core upgrades use predictable, web-accessible staging paths. CVSS 3.1 score: 8.1.
  • CISA added it to KEV on 11/03. WordPress.org's version status API currently marks 7.1.4 as latest, and 7.0.8, 6.9.11 and 6.8.12 are no longer flagged insecure.

A Linux kernel bug you should read alongside these

On 10/28 CISA also added CVE-2026-46300. It is a kernel networking bug fixed back in May, and on its own it needs local access (CVSS 7.8). But the KEV entry says it can be chained with the two PHP bugs to plant PHP webshells and run commands as root. PHP gets the attacker in; the kernel hands over the machine.

2. Who is affected and how to check

These are generic commands. I haven't run them in your environment, so try them on a non-production box first:

# 1. PHP version (CLI and FPM can differ, so check both)
php -v
php-fpm -v 2>/dev/null

# 2. PHP inside a container image
docker run --rm <your-image> php -v

# 3. WordPress core version (if WP-CLI is installed)
wp core version

# 4. Running kernel; on Debian/Ubuntu this file means an update is waiting for a reboot
uname -r
ls /var/run/reboot-required 2>/dev/null

The rule is simple: anything below 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35, or anything on 8.1 or older, is affected. Distribution packages often carry their own version numbers, so check your distro's advisory for these two CVEs.

3. What is still unclear

  • Attack details. Neither PHP nor KEV has published how the bugs are being exploited or at what scale, and KEV lists ransomware use as "Unknown." I wouldn't read "no headlines" as "not affected."
  • Older WordPress branches. The 7.1.4 post says backports to every branch down to 4.7 are "still in progress." I can only vouch for the versions the API lists above; confirm older branches yourself.
  • The upgrade window itself. The RCE happens during an upgrade, and upgrading to 7.1.4 runs the old version's upgrader. The official material I read gives no special guidance on that, and I couldn't read Wordfence's detail page, so I can't confirm the exact staging path.
  • CVE-2026-115560. Details are due with PHP's next regular release.

4. Checklist

  • List every place PHP runs: marketing site, blog, internal admin tools, old project containers, not just the main product
  • Upgrade to 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35, or the distro package that includes the fix
  • Rebuild container images and restart every FPM worker; swapping the package without a restart leaves old processes in memory
  • On 8.1 or older: schedule the upgrade, and get a backport from your distro or LTS vendor in the meantime. WordPress's own post even cites the UK NCSC's advice to consider taking the system offline
  • If you truly can't upgrade today, set session.upload_progress.enabled = 0 in php.ini or the FPM pool and restart workers (ini_set() and .user.ini won't work). The project is explicit that these mitigations do not make an installation safe; they buy time
  • Move WordPress to 7.1.4 or your branch's fixed release. What I do is pick a low-traffic window and turn on maintenance mode, or have the deploy pipeline replace the files directly, to keep the exposure window short
  • Apply your distro's kernel update and actually reboot, then confirm uname -r shows the new kernel
  • Look for signs of compromise: KEV flags these CVEs for forensic triage. At minimum, review PHP files added or changed in the web root since 10/20, for example find /var/www -type f -name '*.php' -newermt 2026-10-20 (untested; adjust the path), and skim the access logs for that period
  • Put PHP 8.2 on the roadmap: the 8.2.35 announcement states it reaches end of life on December 31, 2026

5. My take

Two things stood out to me over these two weeks.

First, KEV is a better priority list than CVSS scores. A small team can't chase every CVE, but "already exploited" is worth dropping other work for. Subscribing to the KEV feed and reading it once a week costs almost nothing.

Second, a single bug's score understates a chain. That kernel bug was fixed in May and, on its own, is a local privilege escalation. On hosts without a regular reboot routine, it became the last link of an attack chain in October. Updating packages, rebuilding images and rebooting only count when you do all three.

If you want help finding the "forgotten PHP" in your stack, or building patching and reboots into a regular operations routine, book a 30-minute intro call.

title: PHP 兩個 9.2 分 RCE 已遭利用，WordPress 核心也進了 KEV：還有 PHP 的團隊這週該做的事
summary: PHP 在 10/21 修補兩個未經驗證即可遠端執行程式碼的漏洞，10/26 被 CISA 列入已遭利用清單；WordPress 7.1.4 修補的升級流程 RCE 也在 11/03 進了 KEV。整理影響範圍、檢查方式、目前還不清楚的地方，以及一份可以直接照做的清單。
html:
PHP 與 WordPress 的兩週 KEV 連發

10 月 21 日，PHP 官方發布緊急安全公告，修補兩個未經驗證即可遠端執行程式碼的漏洞：CVE-2026-109618 與 CVE-2026-109619，CVSS v4.0 都是 9.2。五天後，CISA 把兩者加進 Known Exploited Vulnerabilities（KEV）目錄，代表已經有實際攻擊。10 月 28 日 WordPress 發布 7.1.4 安全更新，其中的升級流程 RCE（CVE-2026-119977）也在 11 月 3 日進了 KEV。

很多團隊會說「我們不是 PHP 公司」。但我在客戶那邊最常看到的是：產品用 Node 或 Go 寫，官網、部落格、活動頁卻是一台 WordPress；或是某個早期的 Laravel 後台、phpMyAdmin 還開著。最容易出事的，往往是大家忘記還在跑的那台。

一、到底發生什麼事

PHP 本身（10/20–10/26）

  • 10/20 官方預告隔天 14:00 UTC 會發布修補，並說明兩個漏洞都是 CVSS v4.0 9.2。
  • 10/21 發布 8.5.12、8.4.27、8.3.36、8.2.35。兩個漏洞分別是記憶體不足（OOM）處理中斷時造成的狀態損壞，以及請求結束後殘留的內部狀態被下一個請求誤用。
  • 官方說明影響所有對外服務 HTTP 請求的 PHP：PHP-FPM、Apache mod_php、php-cgi、FrankenPHP、LiteSpeed 都算在內，其中 mod_php 風險最高。
  • PHP 8.1 以前的版本官方不再修補。安全團隊在 php-src 放了 7.4、8.0、8.1 的最小原始碼 backport 分支，但要不要、能不能用，得看你的發行版或 LTS 廠商。
  • 10/23 補了一則資訊性公告，建議在下一次例行更新前先關閉 session.upload_progress，並預告還有一個 CVE-2026-115560 的完整說明會跟著下一版釋出。
  • 10/26 CISA 將兩個 CVE 列入 KEV。

WordPress 核心（10/28–11/03）

  • 7.1.4 一次修補 12 個安全問題，大部分是 stored XSS，最嚴重的是「升級流程的弱點，可能在升級期間導致遠端程式碼執行」。同一版也更新了內建的根憑證，原因是 eMudhra 中繼 CA 事件。
  • NVD 上由 Wordfence 提交的紀錄寫明：4.7 到 7.1.3 都受影響，原因是完整套件升級時使用可預測、可從網頁存取的暫存路徑，CVSS 3.1 為 8.1。
  • 11/03 CISA 列入 KEV。依 WordPress.org 的版本狀態 API，目前 7.1.4 是 latest，7.0.8、6.9.11、6.8.12 不再標為 insecure。

還有一個要一起看的 Linux kernel 漏洞

10/28 CISA 也把 CVE-2026-46300 加入 KEV。這是 5 月就已經修補的 kernel 網路堆疊問題，本身需要本機權限（CVSS 7.8），但 KEV 的描述特別寫到：它可以和上面兩個 PHP 漏洞串連，植入 PHP webshell 並以 root 執行指令。換句話說，PHP 讓攻擊者進門，kernel 讓他拿到整台機器。

二、誰受影響、怎麼檢查

以下指令是通用寫法，我沒有在你的環境測過，請先在測試機上確認：

# 1. PHP 版本（CLI 與 FPM 可能不是同一個版本，兩個都看）
php -v
php-fpm -v 2>/dev/null

# 2. 容器映像裡的 PHP
docker run --rm <your-image> php -v

# 3. WordPress 核心版本（有裝 WP-CLI 的話）
wp core version

# 4. 正在跑的 kernel；Debian/Ubuntu 若有這個檔案代表更新後還沒重開機
uname -r
ls /var/run/reboot-required 2>/dev/null

判斷標準很簡單：PHP 低於 8.5.12／8.4.27／8.3.36／8.2.35，或者還在 8.1 以前，就是受影響。透過發行版套件安裝的 PHP，版號可能不同，要看發行版自己的安全公告是否已包含這兩個 CVE。

三、目前還不清楚的地方

  • 攻擊細節：PHP 官方與 KEV 都沒有公開攻擊手法或規模，KEV 的勒索軟體使用欄位是「Unknown」。我不建議從「沒看到新聞」推論自己沒事。
  • WordPress 舊分支：7.1.4 公告寫 backport 到 4.7 的工作「仍在進行中」。我能確認的只有上面 API 列出的版本；更舊的分支請自行確認。
  • 升級本身的時間窗：這個 RCE 發生在「升級期間」，而升級到 7.1.4 的過程跑的正是舊版的升級程式。我讀到的官方資料沒有針對這點給特別指引，Wordfence 的詳細頁面我也沒能讀到，所以確切的暫存路徑我無法確認。
  • CVE-2026-115560：完整說明要等 PHP 下一次例行更新。

四、行動清單

  • 盤點所有跑 PHP 的地方：官網、部落格、內部後台、管理工具、舊專案的容器，不要只看主要產品
  • 升級到 8.5.12／8.4.27／8.3.36／8.2.35，或發行版已包含修補的套件版本
  • 重建容器映像並重啟所有 FPM worker；只換套件不重啟，舊的行程還在記憶體裡
  • 8.1 以前：排定升級；短期內做不到就找發行版或 LTS 廠商的 backport。WordPress 的公告甚至引用英國 NCSC 的建議，考慮先把服務下線
  • 今天真的升不了，先在 php.ini 或 FPM pool 設定 session.upload_progress.enabled = 0 並重啟 worker（ini_set() 與 .user.ini 無效）。官方說得很清楚，這類緩解不會讓系統變安全，只是爭取時間
  • WordPress 升到 7.1.4（或該分支已修補的版本）。我自己的做法是挑低流量時段、先開維護模式，或改由部署流程直接替換檔案，縮短可被利用的時間窗
  • 套用發行版的 kernel 更新並真的重開機，確認 uname -r 是新版本
  • 檢查是否已被入侵：KEV 對這幾個 CVE 都標示需要鑑識分診。至少看一次網站目錄裡 10/20 之後新增或修改的 PHP 檔，例如 find /var/www -type f -name '*.php' -newermt 2026-10-20（未測試，路徑請依實際環境調整），並翻一下這段期間的存取記錄
  • 把 PHP 8.2 的升級排進行程：官方在 8.2.35 公告裡寫明 2026 年 12 月 31 日 EOL

五、我的看法

這兩週給我的提醒有兩個。

第一，KEV 是比 CVSS 分數更好用的優先順序。小團隊不可能每個 CVE 都追，但「已經被利用」這個訊號值得你放下手邊的事。訂閱 KEV 的 RSS 或 JSON，每週看一次，成本很低。

第二，單一漏洞的分數會低估串連後的風險。那個 kernel 漏洞 5 月就有修補，單看只是本機提權；但沒有固定重開機節奏的主機，到了 10 月就變成攻擊鏈的最後一塊。套件更新、重建映像、重開機，三件事要一起做才算數。

如果你想盤點團隊裡「被忘記的 PHP」，或把修補與重開機排進固定的維運節奏，可以預約 30 分鐘初談。

title: Field Note | October site update: moving to Cloudflare, a live brand film, blog topics and subscriptions
summary: What changed on the 8plus site over the past month: production moved to Cloudflare Workers, the homepage now runs a live brand film, the blog gained topic filters plus RSS and email subscriptions, and the Lab has new work. Also one deployment that went wrong, and what I took from it.
html:
October site update

The last site note was on October 1. A fair amount has changed since then, so here is a short Field Note.

1. Production moved to Cloudflare Workers

Since October 20, www.8plus.app has been served from Cloudflare Workers, built with vinext. The original Next.js source and the Vercel deployment are still there as a fallback. Why I did it and what went wrong along the way is in this field note.

The same week I upgraded to Next.js 16.4.1 for the October security release; details are here.

2. A brand film on the homepage, rendered in code

The first screen used to be a static hero. It is now a 20-second brand film that walks through the idea, the values, the capabilities and some proof, and ends on a booking button.

It is not a video file. The page runs the animation directly: type, project screenshots and the score are put together in the browser. That means phones get a portrait layout automatically, and there is a Chinese and an English cut. The booking button at the end is a real link to the booking page.

Sound is on by default, but browsers only allow audio after a visitor interacts, so in practice it starts on your first click or scroll. If you would rather not hear it, tap the speaker in the corner once and the site remembers.

3. Blog: topics, a table of contents and subscriptions

  • Topics: posts now sit in six shelves — AI and agents, Web and frameworks, security and operations, engineering and delivery, career journey, and studio notes. The blog page filters by topic, and the URL is shareable (for example /blog?category=ops).
  • A new career shelf: it starts with From a biomedical lab to AI architect.
  • Table of contents: post headings had no anchors, so the table of contents never actually appeared. That is fixed.
  • Subscribe: RSS is split into Chinese (/feed.xml) and English (/feed-en.xml), and you can leave an email to get new posts only when they go out. Both are at the bottom of the blog.

From November I have started writing tech-trend posts. The rule: only news I can read from a primary source. If I cannot verify it, I do not write it.

4. New work in the Lab

The Lab now includes a small office-observation game (Anti-Coworker) and the YES financial management system, and b18 now points to basement18 studio's relaunched site. Projects that have gone offline are marked, so visitors do not land on broken pages.

5. One deployment that went wrong

The first deployment on November 2 returned 500 on 18 routes, including the homepage and the blog. The cause was how the RSS autodiscovery metadata was written: next build did not catch it, but the Workers runtime failed on it at request time. I rolled back, changed the approach and redeployed.

The lesson is simple: run a smoke test on the same runtime as production before you deploy, not just a successful build. Every deployment now gets a local run on workerd first.

Next

  • The shuyan.art creative sub-site
  • More tech-trend posts
